BOARD APPROVED 
27 
 
MEMORANDUM 
JUNE 16, 2022 
 
 
TO: 
BOSTON REDEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY 
 
D/B/A BOSTON PLANNING & DEVELOPMENT AGENCY (BPDA)1 
 
AND JAMES ARTHUR JEMISON II, DIRECTOR 
 
FROM: 
MICHAEL CHRISTOPHER, DIRECTOR OF DEVELOPMENT REVIEW 
 
CASEY HINES, DEPUTY DIRECTOR OF DEVELOPMENT REVIEW 
 
 
QUINN VALCICH, PROJECT ASSISTANT 
 
SUBJECT: 
1-4 Terrace Place, Mission Hill 
_____________________________________________________________________________________ 
 
SUMMARY: This Memorandum requests that the Boston Redevelopment Authority 
(“BRA”) d/b/a the Boston Planning & Development Agency authorize 
the Director to: (1) issue a Certification of Approval for the proposed 
development located at 1-4 Terrace Place in Mission Hill (the 
“Proposed Project”, as defined below), in accordance with Article 80E, 
Small Project Review, of the Boston Zoning Code (the “Code”); (2) 
execute and deliver an Affordable Housing Agreement and a 
Community Benefits Agreement in connection with the Proposed 
Project, and take any other action and execute any other agreements 
and documents that the Director deems appropriate and necessary in 
connection with the Proposed Project. 
____________________________________________________________________________________________ 
PROJECT SITE 
The Proposed Project is located at 1-4 Terrace Place in Mission Hill (the “Project 
Site”). The Project Site consists of six (6) parcels which contain approximately 
14,678 square feet, which currently contains two, two-family homes, which face 
each other on Terrace Place. The Proposed Project is ideally situated walking 
distance from the MBTA’s Roxbury Crossing train station as well as various bus 
routes. 
 
1Effective October 20, 2016, the BRA commenced doing business as BPDA. 
 

 
 
DEVELOPMENT TEAM 
Proponent: 
Bellerose Terrace, LLC – Matthew O’Hara 
Legal Counsel: Prince Lobel Tye LLP – Michael P. Ross, Esquire 
Architect: 
Stull and Lee, Inc – M. David Lee, FAIA 
DESCRIPTION AND PROGRAM 
The Proponent proposed to construct a six-story building that will contain 
approximately 47,792 gross square feet, forty-seven (47) homeownership units, 
including seven (7) IDP Units, and fifteen (15) below grade parking spaces. (the 
“Proposed Project”). 
The Proponent plans to commence construction of the Proposed Project in the 
third quarter of 2022. There are an estimated 60+/- construction jobs contributing 
to the Proposed Project. The total development cost is approximately $15,000,000. 
ARTICLE 80 REVIEW PROCESS 
On July 15, 2021, the Proponent filed a joint Expanded Project Notification Form 
containing both a Project Notification Form (PNF) for the 110-128R Terrace Street 
project (the “Cedar/Terrace Project”) and a Small Project Review Application (SPRA) 
for the Proposed Project, each of which has undergone independent review 
processes. 
The BPDA sponsored a public meeting on August 16, 2021 via Zoom. The meeting 
was advertised in the Mission Hill Gazette newspaper on August 3, 2021. The public 
meeting was posted on the BPDA website. The BPDA comment period ended on 
September 13, 2021. A public meeting was also held on May 23, 2022. 
Subsequently, the Proponent has provided an updated supplemental filing of the 
SPRA for the Proposed Project, and will file a separate DPIR for the Cedar/Terrace 
Project, allowing the Proposed Project to move forward as a small project, in 
accordance with Article 80E of the Code. 
PLANNING CONTEXT AND CITY STAFF REVIEW 
The Project Site is not located within the boundaries of a recent planning initiative. 
Instead, Planning Division staff is considering the neighborhood context, adopted 

 
 
citywide plans including Imagine Boston 2030 and Go Boston 2030, Article 59 of the 
Zoning Code, and community engagement. 
Housing Boston 2030 has established a goal of adding 53,000 new housing units by 
2030, along with providing significant new mixed-use housing and encouraging job 
growth in transit-accessible areas. Additionally, Go Boston 2030 envisions housing 
to be located within a 10-minute walk to public transit. In recent community 
engagement, resident priorities for the neighborhood have included an increase to 
the number of affordable housing, family-oriented housing, and homeownership 
within the community. 
The Proposed Project is in line with the City of Boston’s citywide plans since it is 
within a quarter-mile of Tremont Street, a street which is envisioned by Go Boston 
2030 to be a walking- and bicycle-friendly main street district, and a good location 
for transit-oriented development due to its proximity to public transit. 
The Proponent should continue to work with BPDA Design Review staff to finalize 
the site plan with accurate accounting of open space square footage and the 
mitigation for loss of tree canopy. 
As the MBTA has an existing access easement on this property which supports 
critical maintenance and operational aspects of the MBTA’s rail operations, no 
building permit may be granted until the MBTA’s License Agreement application has 
been reviewed and approved by the MBTA. Written notice of this approval must be 
submitted to the BPDA. If changes to the site plan occur as a result of the MBTA 
License Agreement review, BPDA and BTD will need to review; 
 
 ZONING 
The Project Site is located within the Mission Hill Neighborhood Zoning District and 
the LI, OS-A Zoning SubDistrict, which is governed by Article 59 of the Code. The 
Proposed Project will require zoning relief from the following: FAR: Excessive, 
Height: Excessive, Off-street Parking: Insufficient, Off-street Loading: Insufficient 
and Use. 
MITIGATION & COMMUNITY BENEFITS 
 
The Proposed Project will provide a number of benefits to the Mission Hill 
neighborhood and the City of Boston as a whole, including the following: 

 
 
 
● Creating seven (7) affordable units, which will meet the City’s Inclusionary 
Development Policy; 
 
● Encouraging alternative modes of transportation through the use of bicycling 
and walking, due to the close proximity of MBTA and bus lines and improved 
accessibility; 
 
● Compliant with the 2021 Bike Parking Guidelines, creating a dedicated bike 
room for storage of bikes within the building to encourage bicycling as a 
mode of transportation, allowing for less vehicular traffic; 
 
● A commitment of $12,925 to the Boston Transportation Department (“BTD”) 
to be contributed upon issuance of a Certificate of Approval for the Proposed 
Project to support the bike share system based on a fee of $275 per 
residential unit. 
● The Proponent shall make a contribution delivered to the BPDA to be 
distributed to the BTD to support the recommendations of the Terrace Street 
Study currently underway by the BTD. This payment shall be due upon the 
project’s receipt of a Certificate of Occupancy. The current valuation, based 
on a contribution of $1.50 per gross square foot, is $71,688; 
 
● Creating approximately sixty (60) temporary construction and labor jobs; 
 
● The Proponent has entered into a Memorandum of Agreement with Mission 
Hill Neighborhood Housing Services (MHNHS) to include Master Deed 
Restrictions, which seek to bolster goals set forth by the community. They 
include restrictions to the number of unrelated occupants in any unit, 
maintaining a high owner occupancy percentage, and restricting short-term 
leasing. 
 
Sustainability & Resiliency 
 
The Proposed Project has been planned and designed to support Boston’s green 
building and carbon-neutral goals and to meet the City's proposed standards for 
Zero Net Carbon including the following commitments: 

 
 
● The building will be designed and constructed to meet LEED Multifamily 
Midrise Gold performance with 60+ points, targeting LEED Platinum 
Certifiable, and achieving a Building 2035 pCEI below 1.6 kg CO2e/sf-yr. 
● The building design will pursue PHIUS’ Passive House standards including 
high-performance low infiltration enclosure solutions, and all efficient electric 
heating/cooling, and energy recovery ventilation systems. 
● Installing solar renewable energy system(s) at minimum, sufficient to meet 
common area electrical loads. 
● Assist new tenants/owners with procuring 100% renewable electricity and 
including conditions in the Condominium documents encouraging or 
requiring 100% Renewable Electricity Procurement for future residents, 
owners, and the Condominium Association. 
● Completing and providing updated performance modeling prior to starting 
Design Development and providing Article 37 Design and Construction 
Filings. 
 
INCLUSIONARY DEVELOPMENT COMMITMENT 
The Proposed Project is subject to the Inclusionary Development Policy, dated 
December 10, 2015 (“IDP”), and is located within Zone C, as defined by the IDP. The 
IDP requires that 13% of the total number of units within the development be 
designated as IDP units. In this case, seven (7) units within the Proposed Project 
will be created as IDP units (the “IDP Units”). Three (3) units will be made affordable 
to households earning not more than 80% of the Area Median Income (“AMI”), one 
(1) unit will be made affordable to households earning no more than 90% AMI, and 
three (3) units will be made affordable to households not earning more than 100% 
AMI, as based upon the United States Department of Housing and Urban 
Development (“HUD”).

The location of the IDP Units will be finalized in conjunction with BPDA staff and 
outlined in the Affordable Housing Agreement (“AHA”) and rents and income limits 
will be adjusted according to BPDA published maximum sales prices and income 
limits, as based on HUD AMIs, available at the time of the initial sale of the IDP 
Units. IDP Units must be comparable in size, design, and quality to the market-rate 
units in the Proposed Project, cannot be stacked or concentrated on the same 
floors, and must be consistent in bedroom count with the entire Proposed Project. 
The AHA must be executed along with, or prior to, the issuance of the Certification 
of Approval for the Proposed Project. The Proponent must also register the 
Proposed Project with the Boston Fair Housing Commission (“BFHC”) upon issuance 
of the building permit. The IDP Units will not be marketed prior to the submission 
and approval of an Affirmative Marketing Plan to the BFHC and the BPDA. 
Preference will be given to applicants who meet the following criteria, weighted in 
the order below: 
(1) Boston resident 
(2) Household size (a minimum of one (1) person per bedroom); 
Where a unit is built out for a specific disability (e.g., mobility or sensory), a 
preference will also be available to households with a person whose need matches 
the build-out of the unit. The City of Boston Disabilities Commission may assist the 
BPDA in determining eligibility for such a preference. 
. A deed restriction will be placed on each of the IDP Units to maintain affordability 
for a total period of fifty (50) years (this includes thirty (30) years with a BPDA option 
to extend for an additional period of twenty (20) years. The household income of 
any subsequent purchaser of the IDP Units during this fifty (50) year period must 
fall within the applicable income limit for each IDP Unit. 
As no partial unit payment is required, the seven (7) designated IDP Units fully 
satisfies the IDP requirements pursuant to the December 10, 2015 IDP. 
RECOMMENDATIONS 
The Proposed Project complies with the requirements set forth in Section 80E of 
the Code for Small Project Review. Therefore, BPDA staff recommends that the 

 
 
Director be authorized to: (1) issue a Certification of Approval for the Proposed 
Project; (2) execute and deliver an AHA and a Community Benefits Agreement, and 
take any other action and execute any other agreements and documents that the 
Director deems appropriate and necessary in connection with the Proposed 
Project. 
 
Appropriate votes follow: 
 
VOTED: 
That the Director be, and hereby is, authorized on behalf of the Boston 
Redevelopment Authority (“BRA”) to issue a Certification of Approval 
pursuant to Section 80E-6 of the Boston Zoning Code (the "Code"), 
approving the Bellerose Terrace LLC development consisting of a six-
story building with approximately 47,792 gross square feet and 
comprised of forty-seven (47) homeownership units, fifteen (15) 
parking spaces at 1-4 Terrace Place in the Mission Hill section of 
Boston (the “Proposed Project”) in accordance with the requirements 
of Small Project Review, Article 80E, of the Code, subject to continuing 
design review; and 
 
FURTHER 
VOTED: 
That the Director be, and hereby is, authorized to execute an 
Affordable Housing Agreement for the creation of seven (7) on-site 
Inclusionary Development Policy Units, a Community Benefits 
Agreement, and execute any other agreements and documents that 
the Director deems appropriate and necessary in connection with the 
Proposed Project.

FROM:

SUBJECT: 
100-114 HAMPDEN STREET, ROXBURY (Newmarket) 
 
NOTICE OF PROJECT CHANGE 
_____________________________________________________________________________________ 
SUMMARY: This Memorandum requests that the Boston Redevelopment Authority 
(“BRA”) d/b/a Boston Planning & Development Agency (“BPDA”) 
authorize the Director to: (1) issue a Certification of Approval for the 
proposed development located at 100-114 Hampden Street in Roxbury 
(the “NPC Project”), in accordance with this Small Project Review Notice 
of Project Change (“NPC”) pursuant to Article 80E, Small Project Review 
of the Boston Zoning Code (the “Code”) filed by Green Hampden 
Group LLC (the “Proponent”) on December 11, 2023; (2) execute and 
deliver a Community Benefits Agreement, and any and all other 
agreements and documents that the Director deems appropriate and 
necessary in connection with the NPC Project. 
_____________________________________________________________________________________ 
 
PROJECT SITE 
 
The Proposed Project is located at 100-114 Hampden Street in Roxbury’s New 
Market neighborhood within the City of Boston. The approximately 27,371 square 
foot property site is situated at the intersection of Hampden and Kemble Streets 
(the “Project Site”). The Project Site has most recently been used for construction 
laydown and storage, and is within walking distance of the MBTA’s New Market 
Commuter Rail Subway Station, Nubian Station, and numerous other public transit 
options. 
 

 
BOARD APPROVED 
27 
2 
DEVELOPMENT TEAM 
 
The development team includes: 
 
Proponent: 
 Green Hampden Group LLC 
 
 Mario A. Signore, LLC Manager

Community: 
 CMT Community Mentoring Team 
 
 Bill Moran, Founder & CEO 
 
BACKGROUND 
 
On July 12, 2022, the Proponent filed a Small Project Review application with the 
BPDA for its originally proposed Project, pursuant to Article 80E of the Code. The 
BPDA held a virtual public meeting on August 16, 2022. The meeting was duly 
advertised in local neighborhood publications. The meeting was also advertised via 
the BPDA website and email alerts. The BPDA comment period concluded on 
September 2, 2022. 
 
The originally proposed project consisted of the construction of a modern Cannabis 
Production and Cultivation Facility in a new commercial building of three (3) stories 
and approximately 64 feet in height, with approximately 47,882 square feet of gross 
floor area, on-site parking for up to 24 vehicles as well as a dedicated loading area 
(collectively, the “Approved Project”). 
 
On September 15, 2022, the BPDA approved the Approved Project. 

 
BOARD APPROVED 
27 
3 
 
NOTICE OF PROJECT CHANGE 
 
On December 11, 2023, the Proponent submitted a Notice of Project Change (the 
“NPC”) to the BPDA pursuant to Article 80E of the Code. In response to recent 
changes in the cannabis cultivation market, the Proponent is seeking to make certain 
interior and programmatic changes to the Approved Project. Specifically, the NPC 
Project reconfigures interior space and modifies the programming for the Approved 
Project, with a more diverse mix of Retail Uses on the ground level (including 
Cannabis Retail), a reduced and reconfigured scope of Cannabis 
Production/Cultivation space on the second and third floors and employee training 
and open space on the upper level (the “NPC Project”). The approved building 
envelope will remain unchanged with on-site parking being reduced by one (1) 
parking space (now 23 total). 
 
There would be no proposed change to the building envelope, massing or building 
height, although there would be minor changes to the building façade, entries, 
landscaping, and the like to accommodate these changes. Specifically, these 
detailed changes include, but are not necessarily limited to, the following 
modifications: 
 
1. Added ground floor retail/commercial spaces, including Local Retail Uses, 
Restaurant/café Use and Cannabis Retail Use to the ground floor of the 
building. 
2. Relocated Cannabis Production and Cultivation Uses off the ground level with 
all Cannabis Production and Cultivation now located on the second and third 
floors. 
3. The building’s first floor has been modified to provide for a 21-foot minimum 
ground floor ceiling height in compliance with the pending Code text 
amendment for PLAN: Newmarket, The 21st Century Economy Initiative 
(“PLAN: Newmarket”). As per PLAN: Newmarket, this requirement is intended 
to facilitate industrial use on those ground floors and ensure industrial use 
into the future. 
4. Updated the roof top edge to a consistent level of 64 feet in Building Height 
above average grade. 
5. Relocated bicycle storage space to the elevator new location. 
6. Removed one (1) parking space as the prior site layout did not account for 
the required van accessible space and providing for six (6) EV parking spaces 
on the first floor plan, now with a total of 23 parking spaces.

7. Included turning and maneuverability space at the end of parking area. 
8. Added an improved and additional storefront window system along the 
proposed new retail spaces on the ground level. 
9. Reduced the trailer accessible loading bays from two (2) to one (1) and now 
providing additional trash and recycling in the other delivery bay, which is 
still sized for a delivery truck but will no longer have loading dock access. 
10. Added a freight elevator for moving secured product from production level 
to delivery and movement of staff to secured floors instead of using the 
other two (2) elevators. 
11. Updated the third floor manufacturing space office and fixture counts. 
12. Updated the Training space and the plumbing fixture counts for the 
anticipated occupancy counts. 
13. Modified exterior elevations for new dedicated secured entrance to the 
Cannabis Retail space, additional dedicated secured entrance for the 
building, additional entrance to the bicycle storage space, additional doors to 
access trash storage spaces, and additional doors to access electrical and 
sprinkler spaces. 
14. Added publicly available bicycle locking posts along the sidewalk on 
Hampden Street.

ARTICLE 80 REVIEW PROCESS FOR NPC 
 
On January 4, 2024, the BPDA convened a public meeting. The public meeting was 
advertised in the local paper, was posted on the BPDA website, and was distributed 
to the BPDA Roxbury email list. The public comment period ended on January 12, 
2024 
 
ZONING 
 
The Project Site is located in the Roxbury Neighborhood District governed by Article 
50 of the Code and more specifically within the New Market Industrial Development 
Area Sub-district. The Proposed Project’s Cannabis Production and Cultivation Uses 
are regulated by Text Amendment 479 of the Code as a Conditional Use for a 
Cannabis Establishment. By legal decision of the City’s Board of Appeal, entered on 
April 28, 2023, in BOA#1422422, the Proponent was granted certain relief from the 
Code for this Conditional Use and the Approved Project. 
 
The NPC Project requires no revisions to the subject zoning relief as previously 
approved by the Zoning Board of Appeal for the Approved Project, including: Article 
50, Section 32: Cannabis Production and Cultivation Uses – Conditional Use; Article 
50, Section 44.2: Existing Building Alignment; and, Article 50, Section 43: Off-Street 
Parking Insufficient. As such, the Proponent shall file revised plans with the City of 
Boston Zoning Board of Appeal on Petition BOA#1422422 for confirmation of the 
same via BFA and the same zoning relief necessary to construct the NPC Project. 
 
The NPC Project will also be subject to continuing BPDA Design Review. 

 
BOARD APPROVED 
27 
6 
 
PLANNING CONTEXT 
The Proposed Project lies within the geographic scope of the recently completed 
PLAN: Newmarket neighborhood planning and zoning process. This process seeks 
to preserve Newmarket as a jobs center, with a focus on traditional industrial uses, 
as well as industries of the future. Of particular relevance to the planning process 
goals are the Proposed Project's focus on provision of jobs accessible to Boston 
residents, including residents of the nearby neighborhoods of Roxbury, Dorchester, 
South End, and South Boston. 
 
As a primary production and distribution use, with active ground floor uses, the 
Proposed Project aligns well with PLAN: Newmarket's goal to preserve the area as a 
center of urban industrial uses. The Proposed Project is also consistent with use, 
dimensional and design guidelines from the neighborhood planning process. 
 
MITIGATION & COMMUNITY BENEFITS 
 
The NPC Project will continue to provide a number of benefits to the Roxbury 
neighborhood and the City of Boston as a whole, including the following: 
 
▪ 
Revitalizing an underutilized industrial property site with the construction of 
a new commercial building. 
 
▪ 
The Proponent will work with the Mayor’s Office of Arts and Culture 
Department to conceive, implement, and manage a public art/mural on the 
NPC Project. The public art/mural will be subject to Design Review. 
 
▪ 
The Proponent will work with BPDA and Boston Transportation Department 
(BTD) staff to design and implement intersection improvements at Hampden 
Street and Norfolk Avenue, prior but subject to the issuance of a building 
permit and for a total monetary obligation (by the Proponent) not to exceed 
thirty-five thousand dollars ($35,000.00). 
 
▪ 
The Proponent shall coordinate with BTD, as appropriate, to implement 
Adaptive Street Light Technology at the corner of Hampden and Norfolk. 
Should this work proceed, it would be performed as part of construction of 
the NPC Project, subject to the issuance of a building permit, the BPDA’s 
Design Review and PIC’s ongoing review and approval, and for a total 

 
BOARD APPROVED 
27 
7 
monetary obligation (by the Proponent) not to exceed twenty-five thousand 
dollars ($25,000.00). 
 
▪ 
The Proponent will provide landscape buffering, streetscape improvements 
and maintain proper upkeep of the Project Site and surroundings. Landscape 
buffering and streetscape improvements will be subject to Design Review. 
 
▪ 
The Proponent will improve the setback/streetscape on the streets that 
surround the Project Site (i.e. Hampden Street, Kemble Street and Norfolk 
Avenue), meeting modern accessibility standards. Setback/streetscape 
improvements would be performed as part of the construction of the NPC 
Project, subject to the issuance of a building permit, the BPDA’s Design 
Review and PIC’s ongoing review and approval, and with a total monetary 
obligation (by the Proponent) not to exceed fifty thousand dollars 
($50,000.00). 
 
▪ 
The Proponent will provide public outdoor bicycle racks as well as bike 
storage/ changing room for employees within the NPC Project. 
 
▪ 
Addition of public bike racks on streetscape setback and bike storage/ 
changing room for employees. 
 
▪ 
The Proponent will contribute $4,788 to the City's Bluebikes bikeshare 
system prior to receiving the Certificate of Approval. 
 
▪ 
A parking garage that is equipped with electric vehicle charging infrastructure 
at a rate of 25% installed, or 6 charging stations, and the remaining 17 
parking spaces to be EV Ready for future installation. 
 
▪ 
The Proponent shall make a one-time monetary contribution of Forty-Five 
Thousand Dollars ($45,000.00) to the City of Boston Fund for Parks, a non-
profit organization, to help mitigate the NPC Project’s potential impacts on 
Edna V. Bynoe Park, which is located within the immediate vicinity of the 
Project Site and is in need of funding for ongoing maintenance and upkeep. 
Said mitigation payment shall be due upon issuance of a Certification of 
Approval for the NPC Project. 
 
▪ 
The Proponent shall make an additional one-time contribution of Forty 
Thousand Dollars ($40,000.00) to the City of Boston Fund for Parks, a non-

 
BOARD APPROVED 
27 
8 
profit organization to help mitigate the NPC Project’s potential impacts on 
Edward P. Clifford Playground, which is located within the general vicinity of 
the Project Site and is in need of funding for ongoing maintenance and 
upkeep. Said mitigation payment shall be due upon issuance of a 
Certification of Approval for the NPC Project. 
 
▪ 
The Proponent will employ sustainability and energy efficiency consultants to 
ensure the NPC Project is designed and constructed to achieve the following 
targets and is optimized for low carbon emissions and green building 
performance outcomes: 
 
o LEED New Construction Certified performance. 
o Install a green roof and environmentally friendly rooftop landscaping. 
o Includes energy use management and automated load controls, high 
efficiency HVAC systems, LED lighting and advanced controls, and 
water conservation and reclamation systems. 
o Additionally, the development team will contact MassSave to identify 
any efficiency incentives and assess strategies for reducing embodied 
carbon including mass timber and carbon concrete solutions. 
o Prior to seeking BPDA Design approval, the development team will 
provide a performance report to the BPDA demonstrating 
achievement of the targets and the low carbon emissions and green 
building performance outcomes. 
 
▪ 
The NPC Project shall incorporate green stormwater strategies to the highest 
extent possible. These additional measures are to be incorporated in the site 
design in conjunction with BWSC’s 1” requirement for onsite retention. 
Strategies include but are not limited to; bioretention, rain gardens, tree pits 
that incorporate stormwater runoff, porous paver and porous asphalt. 
 
▪ 
On-site program space for employee training and private events. Stipulations 
over use and programming to be codified in the Cooperation Agreement, 
before issuance of the Certificate of Approval. 
 
▪ 
Creation of approximately 50-100 new jobs in this emerging industry. 
 
▪ 
The expected temporary creation of more than 50 construction jobs over the 
length of the NPC Project. 
 

 
BOARD APPROVED 
27 
9 
The Proponent has been supporting, and will continue to support, local non-profits 
with many yearly community donations, as well as abide by the Host Community 
Agreement signed with the City of Boston on October 18, 2018, which requires that 
the Proponent make quarterly payments equal to three percent (3%) of gross sales 
revenue to the City. 
 
RECOMMENDATION 
 
The Proposed Project complies with the requirements set forth in Section 80E of 
the Code for Small Project Review. Therefore, BPDA staff recommends that the 
Director be authorized to: (1) issue a Certification of Approval for the NPC Project, in 
accordance with Article 80E, Small Project Review, of the Code; (2) enter into a 
Community Benefits Agreement, and take any other action and execute any other 
agreements and documents that the Director deems appropriate and necessary in 
connection with the Proposed Project 
 
Appropriate votes follow: 
 
VOTED: 
That the Director be, and hereby is, authorized on behalf of the Boston 
Redevelopment Authority (“BRA”) to issue a Certification of Approval 
pursuant to Section 80E-6 of the Boston Zoning Code (the "Code"), 
approving the development consisting of the NPC Project at 100-114 
Hampden Street in the Roxbury neighborhood within the City of 
Boston (the “NPC Project”) in accordance with the requirements of 
Small Project Review, Article 80E, of the Code, subject to continuing 
design review; 
 
FURTHER 
VOTED: 
That the Director be, and hereby is, authorized to execute, a 
Community Benefits Agreement and deliver any and all other 
agreements and documents that the Director deems appropriate and 
necessary in connection with the NPC Project, all upon terms and 
conditions determined to be in the best interests of the Boston 
Redevelopment Authority

including the installation of new or reconstruction of existing pedestrian ramps at all corners of all intersections

Title 521, Section 21 (https://www.mass.gov/regulations/521-CMR-21-curb-cuts). This includes converting apex

ramps where applicable. Plans showing the extents of the proposed sidewalk improvements associated with this
project must be submitted to the PWD Engineering Division for review and approval. Changes to any curb geometry

traffic signal equipment to ensure that the signal post and pedestrian push button locations meet current ADA and

All proposed sidewalk widths and cross-slopes must comply to both City of Boston and ADA/AAB standards.

the Public ROW.

The approximately 83,470 square foot (“sf”) project site (the “Site”) occupies the 
entire block that is bounded by Herald Street to the north, Harrison Avenue to 
the east, William E. Mullins Way to the south, and Washington Street to the west. 
The Site received PDA designation in 2016. The Site contains an existing building 
at 1000 Washington Street (“1000 Washington”), and a three-story parking 
garage, over which a new life sciences building known as 321 Harrison Avenue 
(“321 Harrison” and together with 1000 Washington, the “Buildings”) has been 
constructed. The Buildings are connected by a one-story lobby and share use of 
the parking garage.

PLANNING & ZONING 
 
The Site is located within the Economic Development Area North Subdistrict in 
the South End Neighborhood District, governed by Article 64 of the Code and 
within PDA No. 106, as created by Map Amendment No. 621, adopted by the 
Boston Zoning Commission on November 9, 2016 and effective November 18, 
2016. In accordance with Sections 3-1A, 64-28 through 64-31, and 80C of the 
Code, Planned Development Areas are allowed in the EDA North Subdistrict in 
order to provide for a more flexible zoning law; to provide public benefits to the 
South End community, including the creation of new job opportunities and 
housing for individuals and families of all economic groups; to allow for the 

 
diversification and expansion of Boston's economy through manufacturing, 
commercial, and scientific research and development uses; to encourage 
economic development while ensuring quality urban design by providing 
planning and design controls; and to provide connections for the South End to 
the downtown economy. 
 
PROJECT DESCRIPTION 
 
The Revised Project consists of the conversion of the existing 1000 Washington 
office building to accommodate new life science uses. The property at 1000 
Washington currently comprises approximately 234,809 sf of the currently 
existing 540,192 sf Gross Floor Area (“GFA”) on the Site. The proposed changes 
will primarily be interior to the Building; however, some exterior changes are 
proposed, including: new thermally efficient windows; substantial changes to 
the exterior envelope at the eleventh floor and expanded mechanical penthouse 
and rooftop mechanicals; increased energy efficiency measures; and minor 
changes to the loading dock. The Revised Project is a separate component of the 
larger redevelopment of the Site, including construction of 321 Harrison Avenue 
in accordance with the 321 NPC. 
 
The Revised Project intends to pursue the U.S. Green Building Council (USGBC) 
Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) certification approval 
process, at LEEDv4 Gold and will purchase renewable electricity and carbon off-
set to achieve zero net carbon performance, which will far exceed the energy 
efficiency of the existing Building and will also exceed the requirements of 
Article 37 of the Code. 
 
The changes to the Building’s exterior have been designed to improve the visual 
appearance of the Building, including the design of the mechanical penthouse, 
changes to the eleventh floor, and changes to the windows due to glass 
selection and frame/mullion color and finish. These materials have been 
selected specifically to complement the materials on 321 Harrison. 
 
The net of GFA additions and deductions results in a total GFA not more than 
the maximum GFA of 542,555 sf allowed under the PDA Development Plan 
(based on a Floor Area Ratio or FAR of 6.5). The Revised Project may result in a 
reconfiguration and/or reduction of several parking spaces in the garage as 
more particularly described in the NPC. No other changes to the Site or 

 
landscaping are proposed. The Second PDA Amendment is required for the 
Revised Project in order to (i) clarify the measurement of building height and (ii) 
clarify the process for approval under applicable provisions of the Groundwater 
Conservation Overlay District in the existing PDA.

ARTICLE 80 REVIEW PROCESS 
 
In 2016, the BPDA Board approved the construction of 321 Harrison as a new 
office building containing approximately 230,000 sf of GFA above the existing 
garage, together with substantial public realm and other site-wide infrastructure 
improvements, including the construction of a new retail space and plaza 
adjacent to 1000 Washington. In 2021, BioMed Realty, L.P., through its affiliate 
(i.e. the Proponent) acquired the Site and filed a Notice of Project Change to 
change 321 Harrison from office to life sciences use (the “321 NPC”). On July 15, 
2021, the BPDA Board approved the 321 NPC and an amendment to the PDA for 
the entire Site to restrict Biosafety Level 3 use and to prohibit Biosafety Level 4 
use. Construction of 321 Harrison is now being completed. 
The alterations from the 321 NPC resulted in a reduction of parking spaces in 
the parking garage from 300 spaces to 248 vehicle parking spaces plus 11 
motorcycle parking spaces, a net reduction of 52 total spaces. 
 
The Proponent filed the NPC for the Revised Project on or about February 3, 
2023. On March 28, 2023, a BPDA-sponsored Virtual Public Meeting with the 
Revised Project’s Impact Advisory Group (“IAG”) was held on Zoom. The meeting 
was advertised in local papers and also posted on the BPDA website and 
distributed to the BPDA South End email list. The BPDA comment period for the 
NPC concluded on April 7, 2023. Subsequently the Proponent filed the Second 
PDA Amendment with the BPDA on June 27, 2023 and notice of receipt of such 
Second PDA Amendment was published in the Boston Herald on June 30, 2023. 
On August 2, 2023, another BPDA-sponsored Virtual Public Meeting with the IAG 
was held on Zoom to review the Second PDA Amendment. The meeting was 
advertised in local papers and also posted on the BPDA website and distributed 
to the BPDA South End email list. The comment period on the Second PDA 
Amendment concluded on August 11, 2023. 
 
SMART UTILITIES 
 
The buildings and site plan will comply with the Smart Utilities requirements 
found in Article 80B of the Code. The Project shall meet or exceed the 1.25” of 
stormwater infiltration per square inch of impervious development standard 
and will incorporate best practice green infrastructure standards within the 
public realm, when applicable. These elements include but are not limited to 

 
porous curb extensions, bio-retention strategies and/or rain gardens. The 
Proposed Project will also include smart streetlights standards for new 
sidewalks, including city shadow conduit and dual handholes in accordance with 
PIC requirements when applicable. The Proposed Project will also adhere to the 
City of Boston’s EV readiness program and shall have 25% of parking spaces 
EVSE- Installed and the remaining 75% EV-Ready for future installation, if 
applicable. Utilities in any city right of way will be designed to conform with 
Public Works Department standards and will undergo further review to ensure 
utility laterals are not in conflict with any landscape design feature such as tree 
pits and/or other green infrastructure elements. The Proposed Project will also 
provide a plan to address relevant conflicts reported through COBUCS if/as 
relevant along William E. Mullins Way for the proposed lateral connections 
shown on the utility site plan. 
 
PUBLIC BENEFITS 
 
To date, as part of the 321 NPC project, the overall project has provided a 
number of public benefits, including: (i) provision of approximately 5,971 sf of 
Affordable Cultural Space currently leased to the New England Foundation for 
the Arts; (ii) a total of $1,200,639 in DIP linkage paid to the City; (iii) $230,000 
paid to the BPDA for transportation infrastructure improvements; (v) a new 
retail liner adjacent to 1000 Washington, including an accompanying 
approximately 4,900 sf “pocket-park”; (iv) and additional improvements to the 
public realm, streets, and sidewalks on and surrounding the Site. 
Because the Revised Project benefits from prior zoning relief granted through 
approval of the PDA, and will include a substantial rehabilitation of 1000 
Washington Street that exceeds the thresholds in Article 80B-7, the Revised 
Project is considered a “Development Impact Project”. The Revised Project shall 
pay Development Impact Project exactions consistent with the existing 
Development Impact Project Agreement for the overall project (“DIP 
Agreement”), consisting of a Jobs Linkage Payment of approximately 
$395,841.77 and a Housing Linkage Payment of approximately $1,976,838.54. 
 
The Proponent will also contribute (i) $20,000 to the Friends of Peters Park (ii) 
$20,000 to the Pao Arts Center, and (iii) $10,000 to the BPDA for redistribution to 
the community at its discretion. The timing and manner of payment shall be 
memorialized in a separate or amended Cooperation Agreement for the Revised 
Project.

ZONING 
 
The Project Site is situated in a Community Commercial Subdistrict in the West 
Roxbury Neighborhood Zoning District, governed by Article 56 of the Zoning Code. 
As part of the permitting and approval process, the Project team will be required to 
appear before the Zoning Board of Appeal to obtain variances. Under Article 56, 
Table B of the Zoning Code, Multifamily Dwellings are a Conditional Use in 
Community Commercial Subdistricts, therefore a conditional permit would need to 
be obtained. Under Article 56, Table F of the Zoning Code which governs 
dimensional regulations in Community Commercial Subdistricts, the Maximum 
Floor Area Ratio is 2.0 and the Maximum Building Height is 45 feet, therefore the 
Project will need to seek variances for those two requirements. There are no Zoning 
Overlays at the Project Site.

as follows:

including continuous insulation, low air infiltration, a well-managed window 
to wall ratio, and high efficiency HVAC systems.

● The Proposed Project will evaluate on-site solar once equipment needs are

Smart Utilities: 
The buildings and site plan will comply with the Smart Utilities requirements found 
in Article 80B of the Code. The Proposed Project shall meet or exceed the 1.25” of

will incorporate best practice green infrastructure standards within the public 
realm, when applicable. These elements include but are not limited to porous curb 
extensions, bio-retention strategies and/or rain gardens. The Proposed Project will 
also include smart streetlights standards for new sidewalks, including city shadow

TRANSPORTATION 
 
The central location of the Proposed Project provides convenient access to public 
transportation (as described below) and allows vehicles to make use of multiple 
existing access routes to and from the Project Site, and has been designed to 
include features to minimize any such traffic impacts. For example, all loading and 
service operations will be accommodated internal to the buildings as more fully 
described below. Parking garage access for both buildings will be provided at the 
northeast corner of the Project Site off of Washington Street and aligned with 
Mullins Way. The Proposed Project has been designed to allow the opportunity for 
vehicular access to be relocated to the north façade of 1033 Washington Street with 
a relocated shared access driveway with the abutting property owner. 
 
The Project Site is well-served by public transportation. It is located within walking 
distance of the MBTA Silver Line, Orange Line, Red Line, and Green Line; Commuter 
Rail lines (Framingham/Worcester, Franklin/Foxboro, Needham, and 
Providence/Stoughton); Amtrak regional rail service; and local bus routes including 
Routes 9, 11, and 39. 
 

 
 
The Proposed Project will include a two-level underground parking garage 
containing up to 353 accessory vehicle parking spaces. In accordance with Boston’s 
Electric Vehicle (EV) Readiness Policy, at least 25 percent of the parking spaces in 
the parking garage will be equipped with electric vehicle supply equipment, and the 
remaining 75 percent of the parking spaces will be EV-ready for future installation. 
The Proposed Project is expected to include a total of approximately 266 bicycle 
parking spaces for building tenants, visitors and guests. Approximately 30 of these 
spaces will be short-term bicycle spaces for visitors and guests. 
 
The Proposed Project will include a separate loading dock within each building. All 
loading activities, including truck turnaround and maneuvering areas, will occur 
within such internal loading docks. Loading vehicles for 1055 Washington Street 
will access the loading area for this building from the Shawmut Avenue and exit 
onto Washington Street. Loading vehicles for 1033 Washington Street will access 
the loading area for this building from Washington Street and exit onto Washington 
Street. No passenger vehicles will be permitted to enter or exit the Project Site at 
the southernmost curb-cut on the site. 
 
The Proposed Project will also incorporate Transportation Demand Management 
(TDM) measures, to be formalized in a Transportation Access Plan Agreement with 
the Boston Transportation Department, to encourage alternative modes of 
transportation, which may include covered bicycle-parking and other amenities for 
bicycle commuters, one or more dedicated car-sharing parking spaces within the 
parking garage and encouragement of the Proposed Project’s tenants to provide 
employer subsidies for public transportation and/or a guaranteed ride home 
program for employees. 
 
PLANNING CONTEXT 
 
The Proposed Project is located in the Economic Development Area North 
subdistrict of the South End Neighborhood zoning district. The site is also located in 
the Groundwater Conservation and Coastal Flood Resilience overlay districts. The 
local neighborhood plan, the Harrison-Albany Corridor Strategic Plan, was adopted 
by the BRA Board in November 2011, and subsequently codified into zoning by the 
Boston Zoning Commission in January 2012. 
This plan was created to inform land use, building form, and public realm 
improvements. At the time the plan was created, the area was characterized by 
large parcels hosting primarily commercial, industrial, and surface parking uses. 

 
 
The plan sought to activate this portion of the South End with a balanced mix of 
active, commercial, and residential uses. The plan created a zoning mechanism to 
allow a dimensional bonus to proposals providing affordable housing or cultural 
space. The plan also required the inclusion of new interstitial streets and 
pedestrian connections, to break down the scale of larger blocks found in this 
section of the South End. 
The Proposed Project is complaint with the use, dimensional, and public realm 
goals of the Harrison-Albany Corridor Strategic Plan. The Proposed Project seeks 
zoning entitlements through the creation of Planned Development Area zoning 
overlay, pending BPDA Board and Boston Zoning Commission Approval. The 
proposed uses anchored by lab and office are consistent with the uses environed 
by the area’s plan and zoning. The proposed dimension and design are aligned with 
the provisions of Article 64 for Planned Development Areas that address greater 
densities for proposals that provide affordable cultural space. In addition, the 
proposed publicly accessible open spaces and mid-block pedestrian connection 
fulfill public realm goals from the Harrison-Albany Corridor Strategic Plan that are 
encoded in the parcel’s zoning. 
 
ZONING & REGULATORY CONTEXT 
 
The Project Site is located in the Economic Development Area North (Area 1) of the 
South End Neighborhood District, the Restricted Parking Overlay District, the 
Coastal Flood Resilience Overlay District, and the Groundwater Conservation 
Overlay District. The Proposed Project will comply with the requirements of the 
Zoning Code applicable to Planned Development Areas within the Economic 
Development Area North. 
 
The Project Site is located on a portion of Parcel 3 within the South End Urban 
Renewal Area, Project No. R-56, and is subject to an Amended and Restated Land 
Disposition Agreement dated November 12, 2014, recorded at the Suffolk County 
Registry of Deeds in Book 53729, Page 7 (the “LDA”). The LDA was amended in 2014 
to allow for the uses currently contemplated for the Project Site and to describe 
the redevelopment of an adjacent development site covered by the LDA. The LDA 
states that the Redeveloper (as defined in the LDA) will not commence 
redevelopment of the “Shawmut Avenue Parcel” (which is the Project Site) without 
the approval of the BPDA and, included as a part of such approval, appropriate 
amendment to the LDA. In order to facilitate the Proposed Project, the LDA will be 

 
 
further amended to describe the redevelopment of the Project Site consistent with 
the description of the Proposed Project herein. 
 
PROJECT BENEFITS & MITIGATION 
 
The public benefits of the Proposed Project include those described below: 
 
Public Realm and Urban Design Benefits: The Proposed Project will transform an 
underutilized parcel located near public transportation into a vibrant mixed-use 
development providing two architecturally striking buildings and an appealing, 
pedestrian-friendly streetscape in an area of the city which is the focus of important 
redevelopment efforts. The Proposed Project is expected to include retail, service 
and/or restaurant uses that contribute to the vibrant, mixed-use character of the 
Washington Street corridor, and as stated above has been designed to advance the 
urban design and development objectives of the Harrison Albany Corridor Strategic 
Plan. The Proposed Project will also include significant public realm improvements 
at and surrounding the Project Site, which are expected to include new street trees, 
a pedestrian plaza, and improvements to sidewalks to improve roadway quality, 
traffic flow, handicapped access and pedestrian safety. Specifically, the Proposed 
Project includes the following: 
 
● Upon issuance of the full Building Permit, the Proponent will make a one-
time “bikeshare” contribution of $164,640.00 to Boston Transportation 
Department (“BTD”) per the City’s Bike Parking Guidelines, as well as provide 
or agree to space for one (1) nineteen (19) dock bike share station on or 
proximate to the Project Site upon issuance of the first Certificate of 
Occupancy. The Proponent will work with BTD and the BPDA to site the 
station appropriately. Bike share stations may require Administrative Review 
by PIC. 
● In compliance with Boston’s Complete Streets policy, the Proponent will 
make much-needed sidewalk and streetscape improvements to Washington 
Street and Shawmut Avenue within and as needed, proximate to the 
boundaries of the Project Site within the public way. Subject to ongoing 
BPDA design review and review by the Public Improvement Commission 
(PIC), Washington Street will maintain a minimum of 16 foot sidewalk 
including at least ten (10) feet clear and absent of vertical elements. Subject 
to ongoing BPDA design review and review by PIC, Shawmut Avenue will 
have a minimum of 14 foot sidewalk, inclusive of a five foot setback 
including at least eight (8) feet clear and absent of vertical elements. All 

 
 
sidewalk improvements are subject to design review and may require 
approval for a Specific Repairs Action with PIC. The proponent should expect 
to enter into a license and maintenance agreement with the PIC. A 
Pedestrian Easement along Washington Street and/or Shawmut Avenue may 
be required. These mitigation improvements must be completed upon 
issuance of the first Certificate of Occupancy. 
● The Proponent has committed to installing or preserving to total of at least 
fifteen (15) street trees in and around the Project Site as part of the site plan 
improvements and mitigation associated with the Proposed Project. Trees 
will be provided in tree pits no narrower than 4 feet wide and 6 feet long. 
The installation of the proposed street trees, in coordination with the Public 
Improvement Commission and/or Parks Department, shall be completed 
before the first Certificate of Occupancy issuance for the Proposed Project. 
● The Proponent will design, permit, and install a curb extension on the 
northeast side of Mullins Way at the connection of Washington Street to 
support pedestrian safety. 
● The Proponent will design, permit, and implement the addition of three new 
crosswalks across to provide pedestrian crossings around the Project Site. 
Two new crosswalks will be provided on Washington Street, one each at 
Traveler Street and Mullins Way to ensure both sides of the Washington 
Street crosswalk provide a pedestrian crossing. A raised crossing confirming 
with BTD and PWD standards will be provided on Shawmut Avenue generally 
aligned with the proposed through-block pedestrian connection. All 
crosswalks will be a high visibility crosswalk to help improve pedestrian 
visibility and safety. Crosswalks may require the addition of compliant 
directional pedestrian curb ramps equipped with tactile warning strips. All 
crosswalks and pedestrian ramps must be designed with review from the 
Disabilities Commission, PWD, BTD, and BPDA. The installation of the 
proposed crosswalks shall be completed before the first Certificate of 
Occupancy issuance for the Proposed Project. 
● In anticipation of vehicle demand and vehicle/pedestrian conflicts resulting 
from the Proposed Project, the City may require the addition of signal 
control at the Washington Street/William E Mullins Way intersection subject 
to further review by BPDA and the Boston Transportation Department. If 
required as aforesaid, the Proposed Project will design and implement a 
new signalized intersection at Mullins Way and Washington Street, subject to 
receipt of necessary permits and approvals. 
● In the future, the garage entrance to the below-grade vehicle parking garage 
might be relocated to the north façade of 1033 Washington Street and share 

 
 
an access driveway with the abutting property owner (Assessing Parcel 
0306185000). In the event that this relocation is feasible, the Proponent will 
share equally in the full cost to design, permit, and construct this access 
point and will close the unneeded curb cut on Washington Street and 
restore the façade. 
● The Proposed Project will comply with the Boston Transportation 
Department Transportation Demand Management Points System. The 
selected strategies will be specified and codified in the Transportation 
Access Plan Agreement (“TAPA”). For this project, minimum expected 
requirements include minimum of 90 TDM points. The Proponent must 
ensure that the property owner or employer facilitates transit pass 
purchases (with pre-tax benefits, if applicable) through participation in 
MBTA’s Perq Program. 
● The Proponent will contribute $200,000 to the BPDA to be transferred to BTD 
or PWD for the implementation of transit infrastructure, safety, or public 
realm improvements in the vicinity of the Project Site. This contribution is 
due upon receipt of the first Certificate of Occupancy for the Proposed 
Project. 
Subject to receipt of required permits and approvals, the Proponent has committed 
to designing, permitting, constructing (after completion of construction of the 
Proposed Project) and maintaining at the Proponent’s cost landscaping and open 
space improvements on the BPDA-owned parcel at the northwest end of the 
Project Site known as 142 Shawmut Avenue, on terms and conditions mutually 
agreeable to the Proponent and BPDA. 
 
The design of the open space within the Proposed Project must be approved by the 
Boston Civic Design Commission (BCDC), and is subject to ongoing design review by 
the BPDA. 
 
Further BPDA design review will be required on the design of the open space and 
buildings on the Project Site. Submission for further design review must occur no 
later than the design development phase of the Project. 
 
In the event the Proponent phases the Proposed Project (i.e., builds the parking 
garage and one of the two buildings prior to construction of the second building), 
the Proponent shall construct and maintain a publicly accessible interim open 
space within the footprint of the unbuilt second building until such time as the 

 
 
Proponent is prepared to commence construction of the second building. The 
design of such open space shall be subject to review and approval by the BPDA. 
 
Smart Growth/Transit-Oriented Development: The Proposed Project exemplifies 
smart-growth and transit-oriented development by concentrating new commercial 
uses on an underutilized parcel in close proximity to the Silver Line, Orange Line, 
Red Line, Green Line, Commuter Rail, regional rail service, and several bus routes, 
which provide convenient, non-automobile access to the Project Site from other 
neighborhoods of the city, the surrounding suburbs and Logan International 
Airport. 
 
Job Creation/Economic Development: The Proposed Project is anticipated to create 
approximately 400 construction jobs and the opportunity for approximately 900 
permanent jobs. The permanent jobs will result from the proposed mix of uses as 
well as building operations, maintenance and security. The Proposed Project will 
contribute to the continued revitalization of the South End and support Boston’s 
thriving innovation economy. 
 
Start-Up/ Affordable Cultural Space: The Proposed Project is anticipated to include 
within the Project Site approximately 2.5% of the Building’s Gross Floor Area above 
that allowed as-of-right in underlying zoning for use by an existing or start-up 
business and/or Affordable Cultural Space, and provide a contribution 
administered by the Boston Local Development Corporation or Mayor’s Office of 
Arts and Culture, as more fully described in Section 64-29.1 of the Code, or 
otherwise comply with Section 64-29.1 of the Code. 
 
In the event the Proposed Project includes residential uses in compliance with the 
Development Plan, such residential uses shall comply with applicable provisions of 
Section 64-29 of the Code. Without limitation of the foregoing, the Proponent shall 
construct or cause the construction of Affordable Housing in an amount equivalent 
to no less than 20% of the Dwelling Units included within the Proposed Project, or 
otherwise comply with the requirements of said Section 64-29. 
 
Financial Benefits: The Proposed Project will result in significant financial benefits 
to the city, which are expected to include additional property tax revenues, a 
Housing Contribution Grant of approximately $6,344,000 and a Jobs Contribution 
Grant of approximately $1,166,320, all as described in more detail below. 
 

 
 
Non-Discrimination; Boston Residents Jobs Policy: The Proponent will comply with 
the City of Boston’s Boston Residents Construction Jobs Policy with respect to hiring 
Boston residents, minorities, and women for construction jobs.

1. Board Action 
The Proponent (as defined below) is requesting approval of this Development Plan for Planned 
Development Area No. 150 from the Boston Redevelopment Authority d/b/a Boston Planning & 
Development Agency. 
2. Proponent 
The Druker Company, Ltd., its affiliates, designees, successors and assigns. 
3. Project Location 
Planned Development Area No. 150 encompasses an approximately 90,573 square foot (2.08 
acre) area of land, bounded by Washington Street to the east, private property and a parcel owned 
by the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority to the south, Shawmut Avenue to the west, 
and private property and a parcel owned by the Boston Planning and Development Agency to the 
north. 
4. Project Description 
The Proponent intends to replace existing improvements and uses with two mixed-use buildings 
(with an above-grade connection between the buildings on no more than three contiguous floors) up 
to 150 feet in height containing an aggregate of up to 588,000 square feet of Gross Floor Area, with 
a two-level, underground parking for accessory parking spaces, and public realm improvements. 
The proposed project is expected to include a total of approximately 266 bicycle parking spaces for 
building tenants, visitors and guests. Approximately 30 of these spaces will be short-term bicycle 
spaces for visitors and guests. 
5. Public Benefits 
The proposed project will transform an underutilized parcel located near public transportation 
into a vibrant mixed-use development providing (i) two architecturally striking buildings and an 
appealing, pedestrian-friendly streetscape, (ii) retail, service and/or restaurant uses that contribute 
to the vibrant, mixed-use character of the Washington Street corridor, and (iii) significant public 
realm improvements including new street trees, a public pedestrian plaza and public midblock 
pedestrian connection between Washington Street and Shawmut Avenue, a 19-dock bikeshare 
station, and improvements to sidewalks, crosswalks, and nearby intersections to improve roadway 
quality, traffic flow, handicapped access and pedestrian safety. 
6. Project Zoning 
The project site is located in the Economic Development Area North (Area 1) of the South End 
Neighborhood District, the Restricted Parking Overlay District, the Coastal Flood Resilience 
Overlay District, and the Groundwater Conservation Overlay District. The proposed project will 
comply with the requirements of the Zoning Code applicable to Planned Development Areas 
within the Economic Development Area North. Approval of this Development Plan would 
provide the zoning relief required for the proposed project.

Location and Appearance of Structures: The plans attached hereto as Exhibit C 
illustrate generally the location and appearance of the proposed structures within the Project Site 
(the “Design Plans”). As described above and shown on the Design Plans, the Proposed Project 
includes two buildings, with a connection above the third floor and anticipated to be on floors six 
through eight. At the ground level, the Proposed Project includes two “connectors”: An 
enclosed vehicle corridor along the south side of 1055 Washington Street will provide access to 
the loading dock for this building from Shawmut Avenue, and egress from the loading dock to 
Washington Street (as described below, access to the Parking Garage for both buildings will be 
from a curb cut at the northeast corner of the Project Site off of Washington Street). An exterior 
publicly accessible pedestrian connector will extend between the buildings and serve as an 
attractive public space and important pedestrian connection between Washington Street and 
Shawmut Avenue. Key design objectives for the Proposed Project include complementing the 
existing residential and commercial buildings in the neighborhood with attractive, contemporary 
new buildings; advancing smart-growth and transit-oriented development principles; and 
integrating service, parking and loading areas into the Project Site to minimize impacts on 
surrounding streets. 
Subject to the dimensional limitations set forth in Sections 8 and 10 of this Development 
Plan, the final design, massing and exterior appearance of the Proposed Project are expected to 
evolve during ongoing design review by the BPDA and review by the South End Landmark 
District Commission. Any floor plan, floor elevation or other design or use information is 

 
4 
 
included in the Design Plans for informational purposes only, and the final design and/or use of 
the areas shown may vary from time to time. 
8. 
Public Open Spaces and Landscaping: The Proposed Project will include major 
new public open space as depicted in the Open Space Diagram in Exhibit B. The Pedestrian 
Plaza is envisioned as a welcoming space for general public use, and may include outdoor 
seating to support adjacent restaurant uses only in the areas depicted for restaurant use in Exhibit 
B. The Pedestrian Plaza will also provide access to start-up business/Affordable Cultural Space 
within the Proposed Project, landscaping, trees, and other program amenities for the public. The 
Pedestrian Plaza will also provide an important public access through-block link between 
Washington Street and Shawmut Avenue of no less than 30 feet in width from the faces of the 
buildings, and will be designed to allow for connection to an identified future public open and 
green space program at 142 Shawmut Avenue. Subject to ongoing design review by the BPDA 
and review by the Public Improvement Commission, the Proposed Project also includes 
improvements to sidewalks along the Project Site (minimum of 16 feet in width on Washington 
Street and 14 feet in width on Shawmut Avenue), new street trees in tree pits no narrower than 4 
feet wide and consistent with the Boston Office of Green Infrastructure initiatives, and other site 
furnishings, which may include publicly accessible open space, street and pedestrian lighting, 
landscaping, and bicycle racks. The Design Plans show the location and other details of the 
Pedestrian Plaza and other public realm improvements around the Project Site. Improvements 
within the public rights-of-way will be subject to review and approval by the Public 
Improvement Commission and may require the granting of pedestrian easements. 
Consistent with the requirements of Section 64-29.3 of the Code, the footprint of the 
buildings will not cover more than 80% of the Project Site and the remaining 20% at ground 
level will be devoted to the Pedestrian Plaza and other public realm spaces. The Parking Garage 
will span nearly the entirety of the Project Site but will be underground, and designed and 
constructed to allow for the proposed public realm improvements above, including (if and where 
located above the Parking Garage footprint) tree plantings.

11. 
Proposed Traffic Circulation: The Proposed Project aims to create streets that 
become great public spaces and sustainable transportation networks. The Proposed Project will 
have limited traffic impacts due to its central location in the City of Boston, which provides 
convenient access to public transportation (as described below) and allows vehicles to make use 
of multiple existing access routes to and from the Project Site, and has been designed to include 
features to minimize any such traffic impacts. For example, all loading and service operations 
will be accommodated internal to the buildings as more fully described below. Parking Garage 
access for both buildings will be provided at the northeast corner of the Project Site off of 
Washington Street in alignment with William E. Mullins Way. In the future, the entrance to the 
Parking Garage and loading docks might be relocated to the north façade of 1033 Washington 
Street and share an access driveway with the abutting property owner (Assessing Parcel 
0306185000); such relocation will not require an amendment of this Development Plan. In 
anticipation of vehicle demand and possible vehicle/pedestrian conflicts, the City may require 
the addition of signal control at the Washington Street/William E Mullins Way intersection in the 
TAPA, subject to further review by BPDA and the Boston Transportation Department. 
The Proposed Project will also incorporate Transportation Demand Management (TDM) 
measures, to be formalized in the TAPA, to encourage alternative modes of transportation, which 
may include covered bicycle-parking and other amenities for bicycle commuters, one or more 
dedicated car-sharing parking spaces within the Parking Garage and encouragement of the 
Proposed Project’s tenants to provide employer subsidies for public transportation and/or a 
guaranteed ride home program for employees. 
Traffic impacts of the Proposed Project have been analyzed in depth in the course of the 
Proposed Project’s Large Project Review. Mitigation measures to address any such traffic 
impacts will be addressed in the TAPA and/or the Cooperation Agreement with the BPDA. 
12. 
Proposed Parking and Loading Facilities: In accordance with Boston 
Transportation Department’s Vehicle Parking Maximum Policy, Bike Parking Guidelines, and 
EV Readiness Policy for projects subject to Article 80B of the Code, the Proposed Project will 
provide accessory vehicle parking, bike parking, bikeshare facilities, shower/changing facilities, 
and EV parking in accordance with Exhibit E. The Proposed Project will include a two-level 
underground Parking Garage without need of any conditional use permit with respect to the 

 
7 
 
Restricted Parking Overlay. Vehicle parking on the site will be provided at a rate consistent with 
Boston Transportation Department Parking Maximum Policy in effect as of the date of this 
Development Plan, as detailed further in Exhibit E. The Proposed Project may include a 
maximum of 353 below-grade vehicle parking spaces, if the Proposed Project includes a mix of 
research laboratory uses and/or office uses along with retail, service and/or restaurant uses and 
community/non-profit space. In accordance with Boston’s Electric Vehicle (EV) Readiness 
Policy and Exhibit E, at least 25 percent of the parking spaces in the Parking Garage will be 
equipped with electric vehicle supply equipment, and the remaining 75 percent of the parking 
spaces will be EV-ready for future installation. 
As currently contemplated, the Proposed Project is expected to include a total of 
approximately 266 bicycle parking spaces for building tenants, visitors and guests. 
Approximately 30 of these spaces will be short-term bicycle spaces for visitors and guests. The 
anticipated locations for bicycle parking are shown on the Site Plan. 
As stated above, the Proposed Project is expected to include a separate loading dock 
within each building, consisting of approximately two truck bays for deliveries and a trash 
compactor/dumpster in each loading dock. All loading activities, including truck turnaround and 
maneuvering areas, will occur within such internal loading docks. Loading vehicles for 1055 
Washington Street will access the loading area for this building from the Shawmut Avenue and 
exit onto Washington Street. Loading vehicles for 1033 Washington Street will access the 
loading area for this building from Washington Street and exit onto Washington Street.

37, Green Buildings, of the Code. The Proposed Project shall also comply with Article 25A,

Conservation Overlay District, of the Code, as more fully described below. 
 
The Proposed Project will additionally achieve the following: 
 
Sustainable Development 
• 
Set carbon reduction standards for new buildings and emphasize passive strategies 
that address multiple benefits including carbon reduction, and climate change 
preparedness and zero net carbon strategies 
• 
Set LEED for (Core and Shell version 4) Gold as a minimum standard to ensure 
comprehensive sustainability at the district and neighborhood scale. 
• 
All new buildings should include innovative strategies and technologies for building-
integrated and on-site renewable energy. 

 
8 
 
• 
All new street configurations and buildings should be sited to optimize building solar 
orientation. 
Preparedness & Resiliency 
 
• 
Through building and site design, ensure preparedness for the effects of climate 
change including sea level rise, heat waves, and severe storms. 
 
Infrastructure 
 
• 
All associated infrastructure (including laterals needed for future development 
phases) are to be provided during the construction of new street networks. 
• 
Through site and green infrastructure design, limit pollution and disruption of 
the natural hydrologic system by managing storm water volume and flow 
through structural and non-structural means including landscaping, groundwater 
infiltration and vegetated roofs. 
• 
Minimize heat island effect with open space, vegetated roofs, cool roofs and 
hardscape materials with a solar reflectance index (SRI) of at least 29. 
• 
Minimize the area of paved surface so that it is no greater than necessary to meet 
the needs of existing and new uses. 
 
The Proposed Project will comply with the standards and requirements set forth in Article 
32 of the Code. The Proponent shall obtain a written determination from the Boston Water and 
Sewer Commission (“BWSC”) as to whether the Proposed Project meets the standards and 
requirements of said Article 32. In addition, the Proponent shall demonstrate that the Proposed 
Project meets the requirements of Section 32-6 of the Code by obtaining a stamped certification 
from a Massachusetts registered engineer that the requirements of Section 32-6 of the Code are 
met. The Proponent shall provide both a copy of the written determination from BWSC and a 
copy of the stamped certification from a Massachusetts registered engineer to the BPDA and the 
Boston Groundwater Trust prior to the issuance of a Certification of Consistency. As such, the 
Proposed Project shall be deemed to be in compliance with Article 32 of the Code and shall not 
need a conditional use permit from the Board of Appeal for Article 32 purposes. 
As stated above, the Project Site is within the Coastal Flood Resilience Overlay District, 
governed by Article 25A of the Code. The Proposed Project will comply with the Article 25A 
requirements. Critical infrastructure systems for both buildings will be located at the second 
level of the buildings or higher, including in the mechanical penthouses at the top of the 
buildings, or protected by a passive perimeter flood wall at an elevation of 19 feet Boston City 
Base, which is the Sea Level Rise – Design Flood Elevation.

Public Benefits: The public benefits of the Proposed Project include those 
described below: 
(a) 
Public Realm and Urban Design Benefits: The Proposed Project will 
transform an underutilized parcel located near public transportation into a vibrant mixed-
use development providing two architecturally striking buildings and an appealing, 
pedestrian-friendly streetscape in an area of the city which is the focus of important 

 
9 
 
redevelopment efforts. The Proposed Project is expected to include retail, service and/or 
restaurant uses that contribute to the vibrant, mixed-use character of the Washington 
Street corridor, and has been designed to advance the urban design and development 
objectives of the Harrison-Albany Corridor Strategic Plan. The Proposed Project will 
also include significant public realm improvements at and surrounding the Project Site, 
which are expected to include new street trees, widened sidewalks on both Washington 
Street and Shawmut Avenue, a new raised midblock crossing on Shawmut Avenue, a 
new curb extension at the northeast corner of Washington Street and William E. Mullins 
Way, installation of a 19-dock bikeshare station, the Pedestrian Plaza and publicly 
accessible through block connection, and improvements to sidewalks to improve roadway 
quality, traffic flow, handicapped access and pedestrian safety. The Proponent shall 
complete the required Start Up/Affordable Cultural Space prior to the issuance of the first 
Certificate of Occupancy for the Proposed Project or relevant Project Phase. The 
foregoing plan for public benefits includes improvements to the aesthetic character of the 
development site and its surroundings. The project will also contribute a one-time 
payment to Boston Transportation Department to support the City’s public bikeshare 
system, to be more fully addressed in the TAPA. 
(b) 
Smart Growth/Transit-Oriented Development: The Proposed Project 
exemplifies smart-growth and transit-oriented development by concentrating new 
commercial uses on an underutilized parcel in close proximity to the Silver Line and 
several bus routes, which provide convenient, non-automobile access to the Project Site 
from other neighborhoods of the city, the surrounding suburbs and Logan International 
Airport. 
(c) 
Job Creation/Economic Development: The Proposed Project is anticipated 
to create approximately 400 construction jobs and the opportunity for approximately 900 
permanent jobs. The permanent jobs will result from the proposed mix of uses as well as 
building operations, maintenance and security. The Proposed Project will contribute to 
the continued revitalization of the South End and support Boston’s thriving innovation 
economy. 
(d) 
Start-Up/ Affordable Cultural Space: The Proposed Project will 
include within the Project Site approximately 2.5% of the building’s Gross Floor Area 
above that allowed as-of-right in underlying zoning for use by an existing or start-up 
business and/or Affordable Cultural Space, and provide a contribution administered by 
the Boston Local Development Corporation or Mayor’s Office of Arts and Culture, as 
more fully described in Section 64-29.1 of the Code, or otherwise comply with Section 
64-29.1 of the Code. As indicated above, if the Proposed Project includes any residential 
use, the Proponent shall construct of Affordable Housing in an amount equivalent to no 
less than 20% of the Dwelling Units included within the Proposed Project, with all such 
Affordable Housing located on site, or otherwise comply with the requirements described 
in Section 64-29 of the Code. 
(e) 
Financial Benefits: The Proposed Project will result in significant 
financial benefits to the city, which are expected to include additional property tax 
revenues, and Development Impact Project exactions under Section 80B-7 of the Code 

 
10 
 
consisting of a Housing Contribution Grant of approximately $6,344,000 and a Jobs 
Contribution Grant of approximately $1,166,320. In the event of an amendment to the 
Development Plan which increases the square footage of Development Impact Project 
uses as defined in the Code, such additional square footage shall be subject to the most 
recent Development Impact Project payment calculations. 
(f) 
Contribution for Transit Improvements. Separate from and in addition to 
the payment described in paragraph 16(a) above, the Proponent will contribute $200,000 
to the BPDA to be transferred to the Boston Transportation Department or Public Works 
Department for the implementation of transit infrastructure, safety, or public realm 
improvements in the vicinity of the Project Site. This contribution is due upon receipt of 
the first Certificate of Occupancy for the Proposed Project. 
 
(g) 
Non-Discrimination; Boston Residents Jobs Policy: The Proponent will 
comply with the City of Boston’s Boston Residents Construction Jobs Policy with respect 
to hiring Boston residents, minorities, and women for construction jobs.

Permitted Uses 
 
The following uses shall be allowed as-of-right within the Project Site: 
Research Laboratory 
● Research laboratory uses, including without limitation research laboratory, product 
development and prototype manufacturing (provided that Biosafety Level 3 and 
Biosafety Level 4 uses, as established by the U.S. Department of Health and Human 
Services, shall be prohibited), vivarium, and storage and office uses accessory to 
laboratory and research and development uses. 
 
Office Uses 
● 
Office use, including, but not limited to, agency or professional office, back office, 
shared office space, general office and office uses by insurance companies, cultural 
groups, community service organizations, banks, offices of architects, attorneys, 
dentists, physicians or other professional people, and outpatient medical services and 
clinical offices. 
 
Residential Uses 
• Multi-family residential dwellings (condominiums or apartments). 
 
Retail and Service Uses 
● 
Any retail or service business, including, but not limited to, store primarily serving the 
local retail business or service needs of the neighborhood, including but not limited to, 
barber shop, beauty shop, shoe repair shop, self-service laundry, photocopying 
establishment, post office, pick-up and delivery station of laundry or dry cleaner, liquor 
store, tailor shop, hand laundry, store retailing items including, but not limited to, the 
following: food, alcohol, baked goods, groceries, drugs, tobacco products, clothing, dry 
goods, books, film, video, computer software, art, flowers, paint, hardware, and small 
household appliances, retail uses, including, but not limited to, department store, 
furniture store, general merchandise mart and accessory storage. 
 
Restaurant Uses 
● Lunchroom, restaurant with or without live entertainment, cafeteria, bar with or without 
live entertainment, private club serving or not serving alcohol and/or other place for the 
service or sale of food and/or drink for on-premises consumption and serving or not 
serving alcohol, including outdoor cafes and outdoor seating. 
● Place for sale and consumption of food and beverages and serving or not serving alcohol 
(other than drive-in restaurants) providing dancing or entertainment or both. 
● In a structure, sale over the counter, not wholly incidental to a local retail business or 
restaurant use, of food or drink prepared on premises for off-premises consumption or 
for on-premises consumption if, as so sold, such food or drink is ready for take-out 
(other than drive-in restaurants). 
● Bakery, café, coffee shop, delicatessen and/or diner. 
● Temporary food trucks.
