DESCRIPTION AND PROGRAM 
 
9 Geneva Street LLC (the “Proponent”) proposes to construct a new five (5) story, 
28-unit residential apartment building, with on-site motor vehicle and bicycle 
parking, residential lobby, and utility spaces (the “Proposed Project”). The Proposed 
Project will be situated on a combined lot of approximately +/-14,829 square feet of 
land, which will have an address of 9 Geneva Street, in Boston’s East Boston 
neighborhood, between Maverick Street and Gove Street (the “Site” or “Project 
Site”). The Proposed Project’s unit mix will include four (4) one-bedroom, twenty 
(20) two-bedroom units, and four (4) three-bedroom units. The Proposed Project 
will include five (5) units, or approximately 17.9% percent of the total residential 
units, restricted under the City of Boston Inclusionary Development Policy (IDP), 
which exceeds the minimum requirement of 13%. 
 

 
 
The Proposed Project will include a maximum of sixteen (16) on-site motor vehicle 
parking spaces, including one (1) van-accessible space adjacent to an 8-foot-wide 
access aisle for residents located at ground level. All motor vehicle parking spaces 
will be accessed via a single curb cut via Geneva Street. The number of motor 
vehicle parking spaces approved by the BPDA is a maximum number of spaces, as 
final decisions on parking supply are codified by the Zoning Commission for Small 
Projects. The curb cut size will be limited to no wider than 10 feet. 
 
The Proposed Project will include a minimum total of thirty-four (34) interior 
covered and secured resident bike parking located within the ground floor and 
directly accessible via Geneva Street. The proposed Project will also include a 
minimum total of six (6) exterior visitor bike parking spaces using a minimum of 
three (3) post-and-ring racks in compliance with the City of Boston’s Bike Parking 
Guidelines. 
 
The Proposed Project will include streetscape improvements to Geneva Street 
consistent with the Boston Complete Streets Design Guidelines. The Proposed 
Project will create an accessible sidewalk at least 8 feet in width, inclusive of a 
minimum 5-foot clear pedestrian path of travel and at least six (6) street trees, 
along the Project Site. The Proposed Project will create an accessible sidewalk, 
inclusive of a minimum 5-foot clear pedestrian path of travel, from the Project Site 
to Maverick Street. Together, these improvements will create a continuous and 
accessible path of travel for residents and visitors between the Proposed Project 
and Maverick Street (the nearest public way) and MBTA Bus Route 120. Sidewalk 
setbacks and streetscape improvements will be subject to design review and may 
require approval by the Public Improvement Commission (“PIC”), including 
Pedestrian Easement and Specific Repairs actions.

PLANNING CONTEXT 
 
The Proposed Project is located within the East Boston Neighborhood District, 
within a Multi-Family Residential (MFR) Subdistrict, pursuant to Article 53 of the 
Zoning Code. The proposed development is also located within the study area of 

 
 
PLAN: East Boston, adopted by BPDA Board in January 2024, and codified into 
zoning adopted by the Boston Zoning Commission in April 2024. Given the recent 
adoption of this PLAN and related zoning, the use and dimensional regulations 
proposed by PLAN: East Boston are most pertinent to the Proposed Project, and it 
was reviewed to align with that context. 
 
PLAN: East Boston designates the proposed development site as an EBR-4 
subdistrict. Within this area, recommendations from the PLAN include improved 
transportation and public realm, achieved in this project through the addition of a 
sidewalk connection to Maverick Street and the addition of street trees along the 
new sidewalk for shade and pedestrian comfort. This subdistrict also allows for 
heights of up to four stories for residential buildings. The Proposed Project is 
located in the Coastal Flood Resilience Overlay District, which requires new 
construction to meet resilient design standards. These standards include elevating 
the building above Base Flood Elevation for the year 2070, and limiting the uses 
that can be located below the Design Flood Elevation. The Base Flood Elevation for 
the proposed development site is 19.5’. The required freeboard for residential this 
type of development is 2 feet, requiring a 21.5’ Design Flood Elevation. The 
proposed height of four stories above Design Flood Elevation is consistent with the 
zoning regulations of the East Boston Neighborhood District (Article 53) and Coastal 
Flood Resilience Design Guidelines (Article 25a). 
 
Relative to the East Boston Neighborhood District zoning requirements, the 
Proposed Project will require relief with respect to Building Width, Rear Setback, 
and Maximum Floor Plate. Due to the irregular shape of the lot, relief is 
recommended for the rear setback. The rear setback for the deepest areas of the 
project site has a minimum dimension of 30’ and abuts open space at the edge of 
the Logan Airport property, further supporting the case for zoning relief. Per 
Section 7.3 - Conditions Required for Variance, a variance for the rear setback is 
merited due to special circumstances applying to the land of which circumstances 
or conditions are peculiar to such land or structure but not the neighborhood. The 
location of the proposed project adjacent to greenspace on both the northern side 
of the parcel and to the parcel rear creates a condition similar to that of a corner 
lot, meriting zoning relief for the width and subsequent floorplate size of the 
building.

wherever possible, particularly along Maverick Street frontage.

RE: Letter of Support – Hotel Alexandra, Boston 
 
 
Dear Ms. Simon, 
 
I write in support of the long-awaited rehabilitation of the historic Hotel Alexandra, prominently sited at the 
intersection of Washington Street and Massachusetts Avenue in Boston’s South End. 
 
Designed by the nationally renowned architectural firm of Peabody & Stearns in 1875, the former residential hotel 
remains one of the South End’s most architecturally distinguished buildings, showcasing an outstanding example of 
the High Victorian Gothic rarely seen in Boston. Despite suffering severe fire damage in the late 20th century and 
remaining vacant for nearly half a century, the Alexandra has remained a focal point for both historic 
preservationists and community advocates alike. 
 
The revitalization of this corner and important historic asset will act as a catalyst for the growth of the surrounding 
businesses, as it will drive new tourism and foot traffic to the area. With the addition of a ground floor café and 
restaurant, locals and newcomers will finally be able to experience the charm of this historic building. 
 
As is known, over these decades the façade has deteriorated and the need for restoration is pressing in order to save 
this building. I lend my support in the hope of bringing an end to the building’s continued deterioration, and to 
revitalize an important piece of the neighborhood’s history. 
 
I urge all stakeholders and reviewing agencies to lend their full support to this important project. The time has come 
to breathe new life into the Hotel Alexandra and return this long-dormant landmark to its rightful place as a 
cherished and functional part of our cityscape. 
 
 
Sincerely,

SUMMARY: This Memorandum requests that the Boston Redevelopment Authority 
(“BRA”) d/b/a Boston Planning & Development Agency (“BPDA”) 
authorize the Director to: (1) issue a Determination waiving the 
requirement of further review pursuant to Section 80A-6 of the Boston

mixed-use project (the "Proposed Project"); (2) issue a Certification of

successful completion of the Article 80 review process; (3) execute and 
deliver a Cooperation Agreement, one or more Affordable Rental

Housing Agreement and Restriction, and any and all other agreements 
and documents that the Director deems appropriate and necessary in 
connection with the Proposed Project. 
PROJECT SITE 

The Proposed Project site is situated around the prominent intersection of 
Cambridge Street and Harvard Avenue, historically know as Allston Square, within 
the Allston-Brighton neighborhood of the City of Boston. This intersection acts as 
the gateway to the Allston-Brighton neighborhood from the City of Cambridge to 
the West and is also situated along the Massachusetts Turnpike, where the sites are 
highly visible from vehicular traffic entering and leaving the City of Boston. The 
Proponent’s Second Notice of Project Change (the “Second NPC”) specifically 
addresses the properties known as and numbered 8-12 Wilton Street, 20 Braintree 
Street, and 10 Highgate Street. 
 
DEVELOPMENT TEAM 
 
The development team includes the following: 
 
Proponent/Developer: 
City Realty Group 
 
 
Steve Whalen 
 
 
Fred Starikov 
 
Legal Counsel: 
 
Dain, Torpy, Le Ray, Wiest & Garner, P.C. 
 
 
Donald Wiest

PROPOSED PROJECT 
 
The Proposed Project is a mixed-use, predominantly residential, multi-site proposal 
intended to bring cohesion, new housing opportunities, and modern urban 
amenities to Allston’s historic Allston Square neighborhood. The Proposed Project 
will allow residents to live, shop, and dine, all within Allston Square. It involves both 
new construction and the adaptive reuse of multiple important examples of 
Allston’s legacy of Victorian architecture. The Proposed Project presently consists 
of the following buildings: 
 
• 334 Cambridge Street, to be known as 10 Highgate Street (note that the 
existing building on this parcel is known as the Jack Young Building); 
 
• 16 Highgate Street, to remain known as 16 Highgate Street; 
 

• 2-8 Harvard Avenue, to be known as 1 Highgate Street; 
 
• Allston Hall, to be known as 4-8 Franklin Street; 
 
• 415 Cambridge Street, to be known as 8-12 Wilton Street; and 
 
• Franklin-Braintree Building, to be known as 20 Braintree Street. 
 
The Proponent wishes to convert the previously-approved dwelling units at the 
Proposed Project that are located in the buildings proposed for 8-12 Wilton Street, 
20 Braintree Street, and 10 Highgate Street from home ownership to rental units, as 
well as reduce the parking count at 1 Highgate from fifty-nine (59) spaces to fifty 
(50) spaces, and at 8-12 Wilton from fifty-two (52) spaces to fifty (50) spaces. The 
additional space will be used for additional bike parking and a new, approximately 
1000 square feet community retail space 8-12 Wilton St. The design and other 
details of these buildings, which together contain 244 units and 2,000 square feet of 
retail space, will not otherwise change in connection with the Second NPC.

ARTICLE 80 REVIEW PROCESS 
 
A Project Notification Form (“PNF”) for the Proposed Project was filed on June 22, 
2018. The BPDA voted its authorization for the Director to issue a Scoping 
Determination Waiving Further Review with regard to the PNF on November 14, 
2019. 
 
An initial Notice of Project Change (the “First NPC”) was subsequently filed on May 
19, 2021, in accordance with Section 80A-6 of the Boston Zoning Code (the “Code”). 
The NPC sought to clarify the proposed addresses, number of units, number of 
commercial spaces, and number of parking spaces associated with each building. It 
also more clearly connected the phases of the Proposed Project with their relevant 
sites and mitigation commitments. 
 
On June 10, 2021, the BPDA voted to authorize the Director to issue a 
Determination Waiving Further Review concerning the First NPC. 
 
On June 22, 2023, the Proponent filed a Second Notice of Project Change (“NPC”) for 
the Proposed Project in accordance with section 80A-6 of the Code. The NPC filing 
initiated a thirty-day (30) public comment period with a closing date of July 22, 2023. 
The comment period was subsequently extended to August 21, 2023. 
 
The notice and NPC were sent to the City’s public agencies/departments and 
elected officials. Additionally, electronic copies of the NPC were sent to all IAG 
members. 
 
The BPDA subsequently sponsored and held a virtual combined IAG and 
community meeting by Zoom on August 14, 2023. The virtual IAG meeting was 

advertised on the BPDA website and notifications were sent out to the Allston 
neighborhood via the BPDA’s email lists. 
 
ZONING 
 
The multi-site Proposed Project is situated within three different zoning subdistricts 
of the Allston-Brighton Neighborhood District, Article 51 of the Boston Zoning Code. 
These zoning subdistricts include a Three-Family Subdistrict (3F-4,000), a 
Community Commercial Subdistrict (CC-1), and a Braintree Street Local Industrial 
One Subdistrict (Braintree Street Ll-1). No further zoning relief is anticipated in 
connection with the Second NPC. 
 
PLANNING CONTEXT AND CITY STAFF REVIEW 
 
Planning staff did not further consider the Zoning Code or proposed use as there is 
no change of use proposed and no further zoning relief is anticipated in connection 
with the Second NPC. Similarly, the Proposed Project is not located within the 
boundaries of a recent land use focused planning initiative that addresses benefits 
associated with delivery of residential uses as homeownership or rental. Instead, 
Planning Division staff considered the neighborhood context, adopted citywide 
plans including Imagine Boston 2030, and public feedback to review the Project. 
Additionally, planning staff coordinated with the ongoing Allston-Brighton Needs 
Assessment to consider the impact of homeownership and rental delivery in 
forthcoming planning initiatives. 
 
The Proposed Project is located within the Allston-Brighton Mobility Study area 
which does not address land uses issues noted above and instead focuses on 
increasing mobility for all. During review, planning staff recommended a reduction 
of on-site parking resulting from the expected high-level of multimodal 
improvement use by renters. 
 
The key consideration of BPDA staff during review of the Proposed Project was the 
contribution to Citywide goals of creating transit oriented affordable housing. 
 
INCLUSIONARY DEVELOPMENT POLICY 
 
The Proposed Project is subject to the Inclusionary Development Policy, dated 
December 10, 2015 (“IDP”), and is located within Zone B, as defined by the IDP. The 
IDP requires that 13% of the total number of units within the development be 

designated as IDP units. The Second NPC proposes to convert the previously-
approved dwelling units at the Proposed Project that are located in the buildings 
proposed for 8-12 Wilton Street, 20 Braintree Street, and 10 Highgate Street from 
home ownership to rental units. The design and other details of these buildings, 
which together contain 244 units and 2,000 square feet of retail space, will not 
otherwise change. In the updated proposal, forty-one (41) units within the 
Proposed Project, or seventeen (17) percent, will be created as IDP rental units (the 
“IDP Units”). Sixteen (16) of the IDP units will be made affordable to households 
with incomes not exceeding 50% Area Median Income (“AMI”) as based on data 
from the United States Department of Housing and Urban Development “HUD” and 
published by the BPDA. Seven (7) of the IDP units will be made affordable to 
households with incomes not exceeding 60% AMI, eleven (11) of the IDP units will 
be made affordable to households with incomes not exceeding 70% AMI, five (5) 
units of the IDP units will be made affordable to households with incomes not 
exceeding 80% AMI, one (1) of the IDP units will be made affordable to households 
with incomes not exceeding 90% AMI, and one (1) of the IDP units will be made 
affordable to households with incomes not exceeding 70% AMI.

PROJECT SITE 

 
 
 
The Allston Yards Project (the “Master Plan Project”) is an approximately 10.6 
acre area within the Allston neighborhood. Building E, located at 52 Everett 
Street (the “Proposed Project,” as further defined below), will be added to the 
Master Plan Project by the First Amendment to Master Plan and associated 
map amendment, thereby bringing the overall acreage of the Master Plan 
Project area to approximately 11.1 acres (the “Master Plan Site”). The Master 
Plan Site is bounded by the Massachusetts Turnpike and the Boston Landing 
commuter rail station to the north; the Everett Street bridge and Everett 
Street to the east; Arthur Street and the Boston Landing project to the west; 
and the Boston Volvo Village dealership and a mix of other uses that front on 
North Beacon Street to the south. 
 
PROJECT DESCRIPTION 
 
The Master Plan Project was reviewed by the BPDA under Article 80B Large 
Project and approved by the BPDA, along with the Planned Development 
Area Master Plan for Planned Development Area No.127, Allston Yards, 60 
Everett Street, Allston (the “Master Plan”), and four (4) associated 
Development Plans For Buildings A, B, C, And D, within the Master Plan (the 
“Development Plans”) on December 12, 2019, and by the City of Boston 
Zoning Commission (“Zoning Commission”) on January 10, 2020. The existing 
Master Plan included a commitment to deliver homeownership housing units 
to the neighborhood in either the third or fourth phase of development of 
the Master Plan Project. The Proposed Project expedites this commitment, a 
key public benefit. 
 
On February 17, 2022, New England Development, LLC (the “Proponent”) 
submitted the First Amendment to Master Plan, Development Plan 
Amendments, and the Notice of Project Change/Project Notification Form 
(“NPC/PNF”) to incorporate the vacant building located at 52 Everett Street 
(the “Proposed Project Site”) into the Master Plan Site and construct an 
approximately 150-unit residential homeownership building with an 
approximately 1,950 square foot retail space to activate the ground floor 
along Guest Street (the “Proposed Project”). The Proposed Project is 
approximately 123 feet in height, with no more than 123 at- and below-grade 
parking spaces. The residential program includes three-bedroom units and 
provides 16 percent of the units as on-site affordable units, including all of 

 
 
the three-bedroom units, while generating very minimal impacts as 
described in further detail in the NPC/PNF. 
 
 
The Proposed Project Site is located within the area of and is consistent with 
the Brighton/Guest Street Planning Study, which was adopted in 2012 (the 
“Guest Street Study”), as informed by the height, massing, parking and uses 
at the Master Plan Project, the adjacent Boston Landing Project and the 
Boston Landing Commuter Rail Station located adjacent to the Master Plan 
Site, which allows for a transit oriented redevelopment of the Project Site. In 
addition, the Proposed Project programming as proposed under the 
NPC/PNF, is consistent with the approved Master Plan and Development 
Plans.

ARTICLE 80 REVIEW PROCESS 
 
The First Amendment to Master Plan, Development Plan Amendments, 
Building E Development Plan, and NPC/PNF were filed by the Proponent on 
February 23, 2022. A virtual Impact Advisory Group Meeting was held on April 
21, 2022. On April 27, 2022, a BPDA sponsored Virtual Public Meeting was 
held on Zoom. The meeting was advertised in the local papers. The Virtual 
Public Meeting was also posted on the BPDA website and distributed to the 
BPDA Allston Brighton email list. The Boston Civic Design Commission 
reviewed the Proposed Project and approved the Proposed Project on 
February 28, 2023. 

 
 
 
ZONING 
 
The Proposed Project Site is located within the Guest Street Local Industrial 
Subdistrict within the Allston-Brighton Neighborhood District, which is 
governed by Article 51 of the Code. Section 51-44 of the Code identifies the 
Proposed Project Site as a location for a potential PDA. The Project Site is not 
located within a zoning district designated as residential; accordingly, the 
previously approved Master Plan is permissible under Article 3-1A.a of the 
Code. 
In connection with the development of the Master Plan Project and Proposed 
Project, and to facilitate separate ownership and financing, it is anticipated 
that the Master Plan Project Site and Proposed Project Site will be subdivided 
or combined and that new legal lots will be created and held under separate 
ownership and new public and private ways will be created. 
 
The proposed zoning for the Proposed Project Site will be as set forth in the 
Building E Development Plan as adopted in accordance with the provisions of 
Article 80C and Section 3-1A.a of the Code and may require an amendment 
when such subdivisions or consolidations are created as determined by the 
BPDA. The Building E Development Plan sets forth the proposed location 
and appearance of structures, open spaces and landscaping, uses, densities 
and dimensions of structures, traffic circulation, parking and loading 
facilities, access to transportation and other zoning requirements applicable 
to the Proposed Project Site. 
 
PLANNING CONTEXT & CITY STAFF REVIEW 
 
The Proposed Project is located within the planning boundaries of the Guest 
Street Study. The Guest Street Study created a public realm context for 
underutilized industrial/commercial landscape and required the introduction 
of new streets for on-site circulation and servicing/loading. The Guest Street 
Study also required the creation of urban blocks with complete streetscapes 
to create a context for development and a new district. Since the Guest 
Street Study, the area was also included in the 2021 neighborhood wide 
Allston-Brighton Mobility Plan, which identified key investments for safer 
travel by walking, biking, transit, and vehicles. The Proposed Project will 
advance goals of both of these plans by providing improved streetscape 
along Everett Street - a key neighborhood connector across the Pike. The 

 
 
Proposed Project also helps advance long-term goals in the Guest Street 
Study for a mix of uses, including residential uses with affordable 
homeownership opportunities. 
 
MITIGATION & COMMUNITY BENEFITS 
 
Public Realm and Transportation Improvements 
 
New Sidewalks 
As coordinated with the Boston Transportation Department and the 
Public Improvement Commission, the Proposed Project will include 
enhanced public sidewalks, furnishing zones and landscaping along the 
Proposed Project frontage. The Proponent will also work with the City 
and MBTA on bus stop locations along Guest Street for a potential shift 
of the Route 64 from North Beacon Street to Guest Street between 
Arthur Street and Everett Street in the future. The BPDA will work to 
facilitate such route shift. If intersection geometry changes are needed 
at the corner of Guest Street and Everett Street to facilitate this potential 
routing change, the Proponent will work the City and the MBTA to 
accommodate this change. 
 
The Proponent will continue to refine the ground floor design to 
minimize the impact of vehicles on the public realm and sidewalk 
network. Specifically, the Proponent will work with the BPDA during 
design review of the Proposed Project to explore opportunities to 
remove the need for vehicle egress on Everett Street. 
 
Bluebikes Bike Share 
In accordance with the City’s Bicycle Parking Guidelines, the Proponent 
will work with BTD to locate and site a Bluebikes bike share station in or 
proximate to the Allston Yards project, and contribute $49,000 to BTD 
for the installation and operation of said station by the issuance of a 
Certificate of Occupancy for the Proposed Project. 
 
Parks Payment 
The Proposed Project will contribute $40,000.00 to the Boston Parks 
and Recreation Department for the operation, maintenance and 
programming of parks in the Allston/Brighton neighborhood such as 
Ringer Park. 

 
 
 
Allston-Brighton TMA and TDM 
The Proposed Project will become a member of the Allston-Brighton 
TMA and participate in the forthcoming AB Link as part of such 
membership (such participation in the AB Link to be capped at 
$50,000), and the Proposed Project will include TDM measures in 
accordance with BTD’s TDM Point System. 
 
 
Affordable Housing Units and Owner Occupancy Requirements 
 
IDP Units and Other Income Restricted Units 
 In addition to the 13% IDP commitments described below, the 
Proposed Project will provide on-site income restricted units in the 
Proposed Project so that the Proposed Project will have a total 
affordable unit percentage of 16%, which is in excess of the IDP 
requirement. The Proposed Project will include a mix of studio, one-, 
two- and three-bedroom units and will income restrict all three-
bedroom units. Such additional income restricted units will have 
income limits of below 80%-120% of AMI to provide “workforce” housing 
opportunities. 
 
Owner Occupancy 
The Building E Development Plan will require that the Master Deed for 
such project have a recorded restriction requiring at least 70% owner-
occupancy for such units. 
 
Economic Development Benefits 
 
New Tax Revenue 
At full build-out, the Proposed Project is expected to generate new 
annual property taxes, and new annual sales taxes. 
 
Linkage 
As described in the DIP Exactions section below, the Proposed Project is 
expected to generate approximately $21,080 in housing and jobs 
linkage funds to the City of Boston as currently designed. 
 
Sustainable Design/Green Building 

 
 
 
Green Building 
The Proposed Project will incorporate sustainable/green building 
design, construction, and operational measures so that the building 
achieves LEEDv4 certifiable, at current LEED standards, at a Gold Level / 
62 points, which exceeds the requirements of Article 80/Article 37 of the 
Zoning Code. 
 
 
Energy Conservation/GHG Emissions Reductions 
The Proposed Project will pursue zero net carbon performance by 
undertaking various energy conservation and GHG emission reduction 
strategies to achieve a Building 2035 predictive carbon emission 
intensity (pCEI) of 1.8 kg CO2e / sf-yr including: 
i. Incorporation of a high-performance building envelope. 
ii. Incorporation of all-electric heating, cooling and hot water 
systems for the residential uses in the building. 
iii. Incorporation of an approximately 26 kW rooftop PV solar array. 
iv. Subscribe to Boston Community Choice Electricity ‘Green 100’ 
100% renewable electricity for common area electricity needs 
not met by the solar PV array. 
v. Initial set up of individual unit electrical subscribing to Boston 
Community Choice Electricity ‘Green 100’ 100% renewable 
electricity and informing unit owners of the buildings zero 
carbon goals, benefits of using renewable electricity, and 
program options. 
vi. Providing 25% Electric Vehicle (EV) charging stations for non-
short term parking spaces. An additional 75% of such spaces 
will be EV ready, to further reduce GHG emissions associated 
with vehicles. 
 
SMART UTILITIES 
 
● The Proposed Project complies with Smart Utilities stormwater 
infiltration requirements. In accordance with Smart Utilities policy for 
projects with GSF exceeding 100,000 square feet, the Proponent has 
committed to 1.25” of infiltration per square inch of impervious 
development. Green Infrastructure such as bioretention, green roofs 
and permeable pavers and best practice concepts shall be considered 

 
 
● On-going review of horizontal infrastructure and landscape features 
along Guest Street and Everett St. Proper distances shall be 
maintained from tree-pits for all horizontal infrastructure. 
● Verification of compliance with the City of Boston EV Readiness Policy 
for New Developments, including EV chargers and needed 
infrastructure. The Proposed Project shall have 25% of parking spaces 
be EVSE-Installed; and the remaining 75% of parking spaces shall be 
EV-Ready for future installation, to the maximum extent practicable. 
Transformers are to be sized to accommodate future loads.

units in the Proposed Project, cannot be stacked or concentrated on the 
same floors, and must be consistent in bedroom count with the entire 
Proposed Project. 
 
The AHA for the Proposed Project must be executed along with, or prior to, 
the issuance of the Certification of Compliance and the Certification of 
Consistency for the Proposed Project. The Proponent must register each 
building within the Proposed Project with the Boston Fair Housing 
Commission (“BFHC”) upon issuance of the building permit. The IDP Units will 
not be marketed prior to the submission and approval of an Affirmative 
Marketing Plan by the BIFHDC and the BPDA (the “Marketing Plan”). 
Preference will be given to applicants who meet the following criteria, 
weighted in the order below: 
 
(1) Boston resident; 
(2) Household size (a minimum of one (1) person per bedroom); 
(3) First time homebuyer; and 
(4) First generation homebuyer. 
 
The IDP Units will not be marketed prior to the submission and approval of 
the Marketing Plan. A deed restriction will be placed on each of the IDP Units 
to maintain affordability for a total period of fifty (50) years (this includes 
thirty (30) years with a BPDA option to extend for an additional period of 
twenty (20) years). The household income of the buyer and sales price of any 
subsequent sale of the IDP Units during this fifty (50) year period must fall 
within the applicable income and sales price limits for each IDP Unit. IDP 
Units may not be rented out by the developer prior to sale to an income 
eligible buyer, and the BPDA or its assigns or successors will monitor the 
ongoing affordability of the IDP Units. 
In addition, if number of units is reduced during construction plan 
refinement and the calculation of the ownership IDP on-site commitment for 
the Proposed Project results in a remainder of 0.5 or less, the Proponent will 

 
 
be required to make a partial unit IDP contribution to the IDP Special 
Revenue Fund (“IDP Fund”), held by the City of Boston Treasury Department, 
and managed by the City of Boston Department or Neighborhood 
Development in an amount equal to the remainder multiplied by $300,000 
(e.g. the Zone B Contribution Factor). This payment will be made at the time 
of the building permit for such building.

FIRST AMENDMENT TO BUILDING A DEVELOPMENT PLAN 
FOR 
PLANNED DEVELOPMENT AREA NO. 127 
ALLSTON YARDS, ALLSTON 
Dated: March 16, 2023 
Pursuant to Section 3-1A and Article 80C of the Zoning Code of the City of Boston (the 
“Code”), this amendment constitutes the First Amendment to the Building A Development Plan 
for Planned Development Area No. 127 (the “First Amendment”). 
1. 
The PDA Development Plan Background. On December 12, 2019, the Boston 
Redevelopment Authority, d/b/a the Boston Planning & Development Agency (“BPDA”) 
approved an amendment to the maps entitled “Zoning Districts City of Boston” to establish 
boundaries for Planned Development Area No. 127, and a Master Plan for Planned Development 
Area No. 127 (the “Original Master Plan”), and also approved a Building A Development Plan 
for Planned Development Area No. 127 (the “Development Plan”). On January 8, 2020, the 
Boston Zoning Commission (the “Commission”) approved the map amendment, the Original 
Master Plan (as amended by that certain First Amendment to Master Plan for Planned 
Development Area No. 127 approved herewith, and together with the Original Master Plan, 
collectively, the “Master Plan”) and the Development Plan, which became effective on January 
10, 2020. The Development Plan provides for the construction of Building A as part of the 
Master Project (as defined in the Master Plan) on an existing approximately 2.93-acre portion of 
the larger Master Plan PDA Area (as defined in the Master Plan) (the “Project”). Capitalized 
terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings assigned to such terms in the 
Development Plan. 
2. 
Purpose of First Amendment to Development Plan. This First Amendment 
amends the Development Plan to address certain changes to the Project. 
3. 
Amendment Provisions. The Development Plan is hereby amended as follows: 
(i) Section 2 to the Development Plan, which describes the Proponent is hereby 
amended by deleting the paragraph in such section and replacing it with the 
following: 
“Allston Yards Apartments LLC, (together, as appropriate with its successors 
and assigns, the “Proponent”) is the owner of the Building A Project Site.” 
(ii) Section 3 to the Development Plan, which generally describes the Project, is 
hereby amended by striking the words “four (4)” in the second sentence of the 
second paragraph and replacing such words with the following: 
“five (5)” 

 
2 
 
(iii) Section 5 to the Development Plan, which describes the Densities and 
Dimensions of the Project, is hereby amended by inserting the following 
sentence after the third sentence in the second paragraph: 
“The three preceding sentences only shall apply to the Initial Project (as 
defined in the Master Plan).” 
(iv) Section 5 to the Development Plan, which describes the Densities and 
Dimensions of the Project, is hereby amended by deleting the existing fourth

1. 
Development Plan. In accordance with Section 3-1A, Sections 51-44 through 51-
49, and Article 80C of the Boston Zoning Code (as in effect on the date hereof, the “Code”), and 
that certain Master Plan for Planned Development Area No. 127, Allston Yards (the “Master

12, 2019, and by the Boston Zoning Commission on January 8, 2020, and made effective on 
January 10, 2020, as amended by the First Amendment to Master Plan approved herewith (the 
“First Amendment to Master Plan”), for the proposed Allston Yards redevelopment project (the 
“Master Project”) at an existing site along Everett Street in the Allston neighborhood of Boston 
(the “Master Plan PDA Area”), this Building E Development Plan for Planned Development 
Area No. 127, Allston Yards (the “Development Plan”) sets forth the proposed location and 
appearance of structures, densities and dimensions of structures, proposed uses, open spaces and 
landscaping, proposed traffic circulation, parking and loading facilities, and access to public 
transportation for Building E of the Master Project (the “Building E Project”). The First 
Amendment to Master Plan and this Development Plan propose the inclusion of the Building E 
Project to the Master Plan, adding an approximately 20,586 sq. ft. (0.473 acre) parcel of land to 
the larger Master Plan PDA Area (the “Building E Project Site”) as described in the legal 
description attached as Exhibit A hereto, and as shown on the plan attached hereto as Exhibit B. 
This Development Plan also describes proposed public benefits, sustainability measures and green 
building designs, and signage for the Building E Project. 
The first four Buildings of the Master Project, Buildings A-D (the “Initial Master 
Project”), and Building E have completed review under Article 80B of the Code and will follow 
the Development Review Procedures outlined in Section 14 of this Development Plan. A Project 
Notification Form for the Initial Master Project was filed with the BPDA on January 22, 2018. 
The BPDA issued a Scoping Determination for the Initial Master Project under Section 80B of the 
Code on August 3, 2018. A joint Expanded Environmental Notification Form/Draft Project Impact 
Report for the Initial Master Project was subsequently filed with the BPDA on February 22, 2019 
(the “DPIR”). A response to comments on the DPIR was filed with the BPDA on October 24, 
2019. Issuance of a Preliminary Adequacy Determination waiving the requirement for a Final 
Project Impact Report for the Initial Master Project was issued by the BPDA on March 2, 2020. 
On February 23, 2022 a Notice of Project Change/Project Notification Form (the “NPC/PNF”) 
was filed with the BPDA for the Building E Project. On March 16, 2023 the BPDA Board voted, 
pursuant to Section 80B-5.3 of the Code, to issue a Scoping Determination waiving further review 
for the Building E Project subject to BPDA design review. Following the public review process 

2 
 
4842-4928-1277, v. 13 
and the BPDA’s approval of the Master Project pursuant to Article 80B of the Code, and based 
upon that process and the approval of this Development Plan, final plans and specifications for the 
Building E Project will be submitted to the BPDA pursuant to Sections 80B and 80C of the Code 
for final design review approval and certification as to consistency and compliance with this 
Development Plan. 
This Development Plan consists of eight (8) pages of text and Exhibits A-G. All 
references herein to this Development Plan refer to such pages and exhibits. 
2. 
The Proponent. The proponent of the Building E Project is New England 
Development, LLC (together as appropriate with its affiliates and its successors and assigns, the 
“Proponent”).

General Description of the Project. This Development Plan sets forth information 
regarding the Building E Project, which includes construction of approximately 150,000 square 
feet (“SF”) of gross floor area (“GFA”) including but not limited to Residential Uses with retail, 
entertainment, restaurant and/or service uses, and accessory uses. Building E will include 
approximately 150 homeownership residential units, including approximately 24 IDP 
homeownership units (as further defined and described below), and off-street parking and loading 
facilities to meet the parking and loading requirements described herein. 
The Building E Project is anticipated to be a phase of the Master Plan which has been 
reviewed and approved by the BPDA. The Master Plan contemplates the construction of five (5) 
buildings and related infrastructure, as part of a phased redevelopment of the Master Plan PDA 
Area. The Building E Project may be constructed in phases, each of which may have subphases. 
The Building E Project’s design has been guided by the Guest Street Planning Study adopted in 
2012 as informed by the height, massing, parking and uses of the Initial Master Project, the 
adjacent Boston Landing project and the construction and opening of the Boston Landing 
Commuter Rail Station, which allows for a transit oriented redevelopment of the Building E 
Project Site.

size, boundaries and dimensions of the Building E Project Site may change as the Building E 
Project is further refined and implemented in accordance with and subject to further design,

include a portion of the Building A Project Site. Without limiting the foregoing, the development

review, shall be deemed in compliance with this Development Plan upon issuance of a Certificate 
of Consistency.

PROJECT SITE 
 
In December of 2023, the BPDA in conjunction with the City of Boston released a 
Request for Proposals (“RFP”) to lease and redevelop the BWSC parking lots in the 
Nubian Square area of Roxbury. The five parking lots, directly across Harrison 
Street from the BWSC headquarters, consist of approximately 190,000 square feet 
of vacant land: currently serving as parking for BWSC employees and visitors. 
 
The RFP process and selection resulted in extensive collaboration with the Roxbury 
Strategic Master Plan Oversight Committee, the Project Review Committee, the 
Roxbury Neighborhood Council, and Elected Officials. On February 28, 2024, 
Harrison Lenox, LLC, a joint venture between Related Beal, LLC and DREAM 
Development, LLC (collectively, the “Proponent”), responded to the RFP, presenting 
plans to redevelop the existing parking lots to deliver affordable and workforce 
housing and provide creative solutions for homeownership for families, as well as 
for seniors. 
 
The BPDA awarded a tentative designation to the Proponent for the redevelopment 
of the BWSC parcels and a handful of associated, small BPDA-owned parcels at the 
April 11, 2024 BPDA Board Meeting. The BPDA Board Memo outlined that the BWSC 
parcels (ID: 0801854010 and 0801846000) associated with the land area necessary 
to deliver Building 1 (“Phase 1”) would be transferred on or before July 1, 2024 with 
the remainder of the parcels to be transferred by 2030. 
 
The Project Site is surrounded by Newcomb Street to the West, Reed Street to the 
South, and E Lenox Street to the East, sitting at a critical intersection of Roxbury and 
the South End.

Recommendations, such as ensuring front entrances are visible from the public way

affordability levels, as well as the use of public funding to provide deep affordability.

and wealth-building opportunities.

creation of wealth through homeownership and creation of affordable housing. The

improved sidewalks, street trees, and other streetscape features. 
 
The RFP also provides design, land use, and mobility guidance for the development 
of all five parcels as a cohesive whole. Through the Article 80 process, staff have 
reviewed and shaped Phase 1 as an independent project, as well as an interim 
condition that contributes to the long-term successful redevelopment of all five 
parcels. For example, close attention has been given to the height as it relates to 
the existing neighborhood context and the proposed buildings, how the interim 
surface parking can be designed to be replaced with a future phase of

open space can serve the residents of the building for the long-term.

SUMMARY: 
 
This Memorandum requests that the Boston Redevelopment 
Authority d/b/a Boston Planning & Development Agency (“BPDA”) 
authorize the director to: (1) approve the proposed Amendment

37, Prudential Center Redevelopment, in the Back Bay

the Boston Zoning Code (the “Code”); (2) petition the Boston 
Zoning Commission (“BZC”) for approval of Amendment No. 6 
pursuant to Article 80C-6 of the Code; (3) issue a Scoping 
Determination Waiving Further Review (“SDWFR”) waiving the 
requirement of further review pursuant to Section 80B-3(d) of the 
Code for the 39 Dalton Street Project (the “Proposed Project”), filed 
by 39 Dalton Owner, LLC (the “Proponent”); (4) issue one or more 
Certifications of Compliance or Partial Certifications of Compliance 
for the Proposed Project pursuant to Section 80B-6 of the Code, 

 
 
upon successful completion of the Article 80 Large Project review 
process, subject to continuing design review by the BPDA; (5) issue 
one or more Certifications of Consistency or Partial Certifications 
of Consistency for the Proposed Project pursuant to Section 80C-8 
of the Code, upon successful completion of the Article 80C 
Planned Development Area review process; and (6) take any and 
all actions and execute any and all documents deemed necessary 
and appropriate by the Director in connection with the Proposed 
Project and the Development Plan, including, without limitation, 
executing and delivering a Cooperation Agreement. 
 
PROJECT SITE 
The project site consists of the existing, approximately 250,000-square foot South 
Tower of the Sheraton Boston Hotel located at 39 Dalton Street in the Back Bay 
neighborhood (the “Project Site”). The Project Site has minimal exterior areas 
serving the project. The exterior terrace has pavers and is elevated from the street 
level. Access to this terrace and main entry is from existing stairs and sloped 
walkway from the public sidewalk. The exterior terrace is also accessible via stairs 
down from an upper-level exterior public path from both the Sheraton Hotel rear 
entrance and the Prudential Center Arcade Level. 
DEVELOPMENT TEAM 
The Development Team for the Proposed Project consists of: 
Proponent/Applicant: 39 Dalton Owner, LLC 
 
Architect: Gensler 
 
Landscape Architect: Ray Dunetz Landscape Architecture, Inc. 
 
Legal Counsel: Holland & Knight 
Permitting Consultant: VHB 
 
 
Transportation Engineer: VHB 
 
 
PROPOSED PROJECT 
 

 
 
The Proposed Project will convert the South Tower of the Sheraton Boston Hotel to 
student housing. This tower will be separated from the rest of the Sheraton Hotel 
to serve only students. Hotel guests will not have access to the South Tower. The 
first floor will become the dedicated entry point and lobby for students. The third 
floor will be converted to laundry, fitness, study/lounge areas, and resident life 
services for the students. 
 
The Proposed Project also includes a redesign of the existing plaza to introduce 
dense planting, including a row of trees running along the back of the Belvedere 
Street sidewalk, other tree locations, and low plantings to augment existing site 
infrastructure. Additionally, a variety of seating is proposed to create a comfortable, 
dedicated outdoor space for the students living in the dorm, which will have the 
effect of improving the visibility from the public sidewalk. The proposed site plan 
also incorporates proposed accommodations that build in improved walking and 
biking facilities for neighbor/student/visitor use and safety, including shortened 
crosswalks, separated bike lanes, visitor bike racks, and a year-round bikeshare 
station.

PLANNING CONTEXT 
The Proposed Project is proposed within Amendment No. 6, to the original 
Development Plan for Planned Development Area No. 37, the Prudential Center 
Redevelopment (“PDA No. 37”) which was approved by the Boston Zoning 
Commission and made effective March 20, 1990. The Sheraton Hotel South Tower 
is in compliance with PDA No. 37, as amended. The use regulations in Article 41 of 
the Zoning Code, the Huntington Avenue/Prudential Center District, where the 
project site is located, apply to any change of use within a Planned Development 
Area and allows a dormitory as a conditional use. The proposed Amendment No. 6 
to the PDA therefore amends the list of Permitted Uses to include Dormitory as a 
permitted Institutional Use. Any Institutional user of the dormitory is required to 
identify the location of such use in its Institutional Master Plan. In addition to the 
Proposed Project’s consistency with PDA No. 37, as amended and the use 
regulations of Article 41, the conversion of underutilized hotel space into an 
undergraduate dormitory supports the Housing Boston 2030 goal of increasing 
new off-campus student dormitory housing to relieve market pressure on Boston’s 
housing market. 
 
ZONING & REGULATORY CONTEXT 
The Proposed Project is located within the Huntington Avenue/Prudential Center 
District, identified on Map 1D of the Zoning District Maps of the City of Boston and 
is subject to Article 41 of the Boston Zoning Code (the "Code"). As referenced on 
Map 1D, the Proposed Project is also located within PDA No. 37, as amended. The 

 
 
Project Site is not located within any of the three Huntington Avenue/Prudential 
Center District Protection Areas as described in Article 41-5 of the Code. 
Pursuant to Subsection 1 of Article 41-12 of the Code, Article 41-17 entitled 
"Huntington Avenue/Prudential Center District Use Regulations" shall apply to any 
change of use within a Planned Development Area for which a building or use 
permit is required. Article 41-17 allows dormitory as a conditional use. 
As evidenced in section XII. Developer Impact Project Contributions of PDA No. 37, 
the original Prudential Center Redevelopment Project complied with the Daycare 
provision of Article 41-17 by providing 14,800 square feet of on-site childcare 
centers, therefore the Proposed Project has complied with such provision. 
The Proponent seeks to add dormitory as a permitted use at the Proposed Project 
Site by amending PDA No. 37. 
The Proposed Project is subject to Article 80B review by the Boston Planning and 
Development Agency (the "BPDA"). Within the Downtown District (which includes 
the Huntington Avenue/Prudential Center District), Article 80B Large Project Review 
applies to, inter alia, any project "to establish or change the uses of a gross floor 
area of one hundred thousand (100,000) or more square feet." As the South Tower 
gross floor area exceeds one hundred thousand (100,000) square feet, the change 
in use contemplated by the Proposed Project triggers Article 80B review. 
The change in use is accomplished through Amendment No. 6 to include dormitory 
as a permitted Institutional use in the Planned Development Area. Any Institutional 
user of the dormitory is required to identify the location of such use in its 
Institutional Master Plan. 
PROJECT BENEFITS AND MITIGATION 
As will be further defined in the Cooperation Agreement, the Proposed Project will 
provide the following benefits for the city and the neighborhood: 
Housing 
● The Proposed Project will help ease the demand on the local housing market 
by providing dedicated student housing for approximately 856 students. 
Urban Design/Public Realm 
● See Exhibit B for the project site plan. 

 
 
● The new, dedicated, dormitory entrance will be located in the second bay 
from the west at the plaza level. 
● New entry-level signage will mark the building as part of Northeastern 
University. 
● Significant planting including trees will be installed and maintained at the 
plaza level. 
● The Proponent will contribute $117,700 as a bikeshare contribution, 
consistent with the Bike Parking Guidelines. 
● The Proponent will contribute $266,000 for off-site safety and accessibility 
improvements to Belvidere Street and Dalton Street, which are elaborated 
upon in the Transportation section below. 
Sustainability/Environmental 
● The work on the plaza area will work to mitigate the urban heat island effect 
by the following: 
○ Adding green planted areas with trees where previously there was just 
gravel; 
○ Adding more planted areas than the current configuration; 
○ Adding a canopy to the entry of the building; and 
○ Adding umbrellas at the site furniture on the plaza. 
RESILIENCY AND SUSTAINABILITY 
Article 37 Sustainability Requirements: 
The Proposed Project will achieve LEED Certifiability 
Smart Utilities: 
The Proposed Project has indicated that existing systems and services will remain 
intact and no new infrastructure is anticipated. Should any significant updates to 
the building systems and related infrastructure occur, the Proponent agrees to 
complete the Smart Utilities review prior to obtaining a Certificate of Occupancy. 
INCLUSIONARY DEVELOPMENT POLICY 

 
 
The Inclusionary Development Policy (“IDP”), dated December 10, 2015, exempts 
any Proposed Projects from IDP requirements if the Project is: (a) financed as one 
entity and provides 40% or more of units within the project as income-restricted, (b) 
a dormitory, or (c) an otherwise exempt site usage under the Zoning Code. As such, 
the Proposed Project, as a dormitory, is exempt from obligations under the IDP. 
TRANSPORTATION 
Pedestrian access to the Proposed Project will occur via brick sidewalks and an 
existing brick plaza on Belvidere Street. The plaza sits above the street and is 
accessed by a combined stairway and ramp structure. The Proposed Project will 
improve the existing plaza with plantings, seating, bike racks, and, in coordination 
with the BPDA, Boston Transportation Department (“BTD”), and Disabilities 
Commission, accessibility improvements to ensure surfaces and slopes are 
compliant with contemporary access requirements. 
No motor vehicle parking will be provided on-site. The Proposed Project is 
anchored to the existing Prudential Center parking garage, which is accessed via 
Belvidere Street. This existing garage and curb cut will provide access and egress to 
on-site service and loading areas as well as publicly accessible motor vehicle 
parking. 
The Proposed Project will include a minimum total of fifty-seven (57) interior 
covered and secured resident bike parking spaces located in the ground floor. In 
recognition that the quantity of resident bike parking spaces does not meet 
minimum guidelines, the proponent will provide in-room bicycle racks to residents, 
upon request, which will be coordinated through the Institution’s facilities 
management team. The in-room bike rack specifications will be selected in 
consultation with the BPDA and BTD to best align with the City of Boston Bike 
Parking Guidelines. The Proposed Project will also include a minimum total of eight 
(8) exterior visitor bike parking spaces using a minimum of four (4) post-and-ring 
racks in compliance with the guidelines. 
Within thirty (30) days of approval of the PDA Amendment, the Proponent will make 
a one-time “bikeshare” contribution of $117,000.00 to BTD per the City of Boston 
Bike Parking Guidelines as well as provide space for one (1) 47-dock year-round 
bikeshare station onsite. The proponent will work with BTD and the BPDA to site 
the station, which is anticipated to be located along the north side of Belvidere 
Street immediately adjacent to the Proposed Project. The station will be connected 
to the electrical grid to support e-bike charging as part of the bikeshare system. 

 
 
Within thirty (30) days of approval of the PDA Amendment by the Boston Zoning 
Commission, the Proponent will make a one-time contribution in the amount of two 
hundred and fifty-six thousand ($256,000.00) dollars toward off-site safety and 
accessibility improvements to Belvidere Street and Dalton Street in the vicinity of 
the Project site. Such funding shall be managed by the BPDA, BTD and PWD and 
may be allocated to design and/or build out of such improvements, as follows: 
● Design work to produce plans for safety and accessibility improvements to 
Belvidere Street and Dalton Street that enable safe, comfortable, and 
accessible travel between the Proposed Project, nearby institutions, and area 
destinations. These improvements can include, but are not limited to, ADA 
compliant pedestrian ramps, paths of travel, and crosswalks; separated bike 
lanes; a floating bus stop on Belvidere Street; a raised concrete island for the 
year-round operation of the 47-dock bikeshare station; and, as needed, 
changes to curbside regulations on Belvidere Street and Dalton Street. As 
shown in Exhibit A, the limits of this work will be located between the 
intersection of Belvidere Street / Huntington Avenue and the limits of the 
Dalton Street Bridge Project, approximately at the intersection of Dalton 
Street / Scotia Street. 
● Build out of these off-site public right-of-way safety improvements to be 
completed by the City of Boston. 
Improvements to the public way will be subject to BPDA, BTD, PWD, and Disabilities 
Commission design review and may require approval by the Public Improvement 
Commission (“PIC”). In the event that circumstances change regarding this 
mitigation, the BPDA and the City will work with the Proponent to identify an 
alternative solution with comparable impact and estimated value. 
The proponent has agreed to enter into a Transportation Access Plan Agreement 
(“TAPA”) with BTD to articulate a Transportation Demand Management (“TDM”) 
strategy following BTD’s Transportation Demand Management Points System; and 
to set forth the timing for the Proponent’s funding of this off-site mitigation funding 
contribution. 
ARTICLE 80 AND PUBLIC REVIEW PROCESS 
A Letter of Intent for the Proposed Project was filed on April 11, 2023, pursuant to 
the applicable Mayoral executive orders. A Project Notification Form (“PNF”) for the 
Project was filed on August 17, 2023, to initiate review of the Proposed Project in 
accordance with Article 80B Large Project Review of the Code. Notice of the receipt 

 
 
by the BPDA of the PNF was published in the Boston Herald, initiating a thirty (30) 
day public comment period. 
On August 14, 2023, the Proponent submitted Amendment No. 6 for review, which 
initiated a forty-five (45) day public comment period to conclude on October 2, 
2023. Notice of the receipt of the Amendment No. 6 by the BPDA was published in 
the Boston Herald on August 17, 2023. The notice and Amendment No. 6 were sent 
to the City’s public agencies/departments and elected officials pursuant to Section 
80A-2 of the Code. 
Pursuant to Section 80B-5.3 of the Code, the BPDA hosted a Scoping Session for 
BPDA, city, and state staff/departments on August 21, 2023. An Impact Advisory 
Group (“IAG”) meeting was held on August 30, 2023. A Public meeting was held on 
September 21, 2023.

Development Plan or the Code as in effect as of the date of the Development Plan, without giving 
effect to any subsequent amendments to the Code. 
2. 
Overview of the Site and Project. 
The Development Plan area encompasses approximately 1,116,222 square feet known as 
the Prudential Center (the “Site”) bounded by Boylston Street, Exeter Street, Huntington Avenue, 
Belvidere Street and the Hynes Convention Center. The Site has been severed into several parcels, 
including the Hotel Site (defined in Amendment No. 1). 
Implementation of the Development Plan began in the early 1990s by The Prudential 
Insurance Company of America (“Prudential”). Pursuant to the terms of Amendment No. 1, on 
December 29, 1994, Sheraton purchased the Hotel Site from Prudential and became owner of the 
Hotel Site by virtue of a deed filed with the Suffolk County Registry of Deeds District of the Land 
Court (the “Land Court”) as Document No. 522046 on Certificate of Title No. 109190. The 
current owner of the Hotel Site is 39 Dalton Owner, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company 
(the “Hotel Site Owner”) by virtue of a deed dated as of February 2, 2022 and filed with the Land 
Court as Document No. 931599 on Certificate of Title No. 138466. The Hotel Site includes, among 
other features, an existing two hundred fifty thousand (250,000) square foot south tower (the 
“South Tower”) as shown on Exhibit A attached hereto.

MASTER PLAN 
 
_______________________________________________________________________________________ 
 
SUMMARY: This Memorandum requests that the Boston Planning & Development 
Agency (“BPDA”): (1) approve the Institutional Master Plan Notification 
Form for renewal of the Boston Children’s Hospital (“BCH”) Institutional 
Master Plan (“IMP”), dated November 13, 2023 (“IMPNF for Renewal”), 
pursuant to Sections 80D-5.2(e), 80D-6, and 80D-8 of the Boston 
Zoning Code (the “Code”); and (2) authorize the Director take all 
actions and execute any and all documents deemed necessary and 
appropriate relative to the IMPNF for Renewal. 
_______________________________________________________________________________________ 
 
INTRODUCTION 
 
The BCH IMP originally was approved by the Boston Redevelopment Authority (now 
d/b/a the Boston Planning & Development Agency, “BPDA”) Board on April 29, 2008, 
and the Boston Zoning Commission on May 28, 2008, effective May 29, 2008. BCH 
amended the original IMP several times over the course of the last 15 years, which 
amendments included an extension of the term to December 20, 2023, by an 
amendment approved by the BPDA on November 14, 2013, and the Zoning 
Commission on December 11, 2013, effective December 20, 2013. 
 

 
BOARD APPROVED 
31 
 
 
DOC 8096 
 
 
 
On November 13, 2023, BCH submitted the IMPNF for Renewal to the BPDA, 
signaling its intention to renew the BCH IMP for a period of two years. BCH is not 
proposing a “Proposed Institutional Project”, as that term is understood in the 
Code; is not adding new land area to the BCH IMP; and is not proposing any 
changes to the BCH IMP that would constitute a change in use, dimensional, 
parking or loading elements thereof (other than de minimus dimensional changes). 
BPDA staff do not anticipate any greater impacts from the continuation of the 
implementation of the BCH IMP than were originally evaluated. 
 
INSTITUTIONAL TEAM 
 
Proponent: 
The Children’s Hospital Corporation d/b/a 
Boston Children’s Hospital 
 
Lisa Hogarty 
 
Attorney: 
Goulston & Storrs 
 
Darren Baird, Esq. 
 
 
ARTICLE 80 REVIEW 
 
The IMPNF for Renewal is subject to Institutional Master Plan Review and qualifies 
for a waiver of further review in accordance with Sections 80D-5.2(e) and 80D-6 of 
the Code in that: (i) no new Proposed Institutional Projects are planned; (ii) no 
changes in the Institutional Master Plan are proposed that would constitute a 
change in the use, dimensional, parking or loading elements of the Institutional 
Master Plan (other than de minimus dimensional changes); and (iii) no significantly 
greater impacts would result from continued implementation of the approved 
Institutional Master Plan than were originally projected. The IMPNF for Renewal 
seeks approval of the IMPNF and the BCH IMP together, as the renewed IMP, for a 
period of two years, until December 14, 2025. 
 
The submission of the IMPNF for Renewal on November 13, 2023, initiated a 30-day 
comment period that ended on December 13, 2023. Notice of submission was 
published in the Boston Herald on November 13, 2023. 
 
CONTINUED COMMUNITY BENEFITS 
 

 
BOARD APPROVED 
31 
 
 
DOC 8096 
 
 
 
All community benefits currently offered pursuant to the existing BCH IMP will 
continue through the length of the renewed IMP. 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS 
 
Based on the foregoing, staff recommends that the BPDA Board: (1) approve the 
IMPNF for Renewal pursuant to Sections 80D-5.2(e), 80D-6, and 80D-8 of the Code; 
and (2) authorize the Director take all actions and execute any and all documents 
deemed necessary and appropriate relative to the IMPNF for Renewal. 
 
Appropriate votes follow: 
 
VOTED: 
That in connection with the Institutional Master Plan Notification Form 
for Renewal of the Boston Children’s Hospital Institutional Master Plan 
(“BCH IMP”), dated November 13, 2023 (the “IMPNF for Renewal”), and 
after consideration thereof, the Boston Redevelopment Authority 
(“BRA”) hereby finds that: (a) the IMPNF for Renewal, conforms to the 
provisions of Article 80D of the Boston Zoning Code (“the Code”); (b) 
the IMPNF for Renewal conforms to the general plan for the City as a 
whole; and (c) on balance, nothing in the IMPNF for Renewal, will be 
injurious to the neighborhood or otherwise detrimental to the public 
welfare, weighing all the benefits and burdens; and 
 
FURTHER 
VOTED: 
That pursuant to Section 80D-5.2(e) of the Code, the BRA has 
determined that regarding the IMPNF for Renewal: (i) no new 
Proposed Institutional Projects are planned, (ii) no changes to the BCH 
IMP are proposed that would constitute a change in the use, 
dimensional, parking or loading elements of the BCH IMP, and (iii) no 
significantly greater impacts would result from continued 
implementation of the approved BCH IMP than were originally 
projected, and therefore waives further review of the IMPNF for 
Renewal pursuant to Sections 80D-5.2(e), 80D-6, and 80D-8 of the 
Code and approves the IMPNF for Renewal for a period of two (2) 
years from the date of approval of this renewal vote by the BRA, which 
date is December 14, 2025; and 
 
FURTHER

VOTED: 
That the Director be, and hereby is, authorized to take all actions and 
execute any and all documents deemed necessary and appropriate 
and in the best interest of the BRA by the Director in connection with 
the IMPNF for Renewal.

Subject:
Boston Children’s Hospital IMPNF- Boston Public Works Department Comments
Included here are Boston Public Works Department comments for the Boston Children’s Hospital IMPNF.
Project Specific Scope Considerations:
The developer should coordinate with BPDA, BTD and PWD to develop safety and accessibility improvements for
all modes of transportation in the area.
Site Plan:
The developer must provide an engineer’s site plan at an appropriate engineering scale that shows curb
functionality on both sides of all streets that abut the property.
Construction Within The Public Right-of- Way (ROW):
All proposed design and construction within the Public ROW shall conform to PWD Design Standards
(https://www.boston.gov/departments/public-works/public-works-design-standards). Any non-standard materials
(i.e. pavers, landscaping, bike racks, etc.) proposed within the Public ROW will require approval through the Public
Improvement Commission (PIC) process and a fully executed License, Maintenance and Indemnification (LM&I)
Agreement with the PIC. Please note that the comments below are specific to proposed work within the Public
ROW.
Sidewalks:
The developer is responsible for the reconstruction of the sidewalks abutting the project and, wherever possible, to
extend the limits to the nearest intersection to encourage and compliment pedestrian improvements and travel
along all sidewalks within the ROW within and beyond the project limits. The reconstruction effort also must meet
current Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)/Massachusetts Architectural Access Board (AAB) guidelines,
including the installation of new or reconstruction of existing pedestrian ramps at all corners of all intersections
abutting the project site if not already constructed to ADA/AAB compliance per Code of Massachusetts Regulations
Title 521, Section 21 (https://www.mass.gov/regulations/521-CMR-21-curb-cuts). This includes converting apex
ramps to perpendicular ramps at intersection corners and constructing or reconstructing reciprocal pedestrian
ramps where applicable. Plans showing the extents of the proposed sidewalk improvements associated with this
project must be submitted to the PWD Engineering Division for review and approval. Changes to any curb geometry
will need to be reviewed and approved through the PIC.
Please note that at signalized intersections, any alteration to pedestrian ramps may also require upgrading the
traffic signal equipment to ensure that the signal post and pedestrian push button locations meet current ADA and
Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD) requirements. Any changes to the traffic signal system must
be coordinated and approved by BTD.
All proposed sidewalk widths and cross-slopes must comply to both City of Boston and ADA/AAB standards.
The developer is encouraged to contact the City’s Disabilities Commission to confirm compliant accessibility within
the Public ROW.
Driveway Curb Cuts:
Any proposed driveway curb cuts within the Public ROW will need to be reviewed and approved by the PIC. All
existing curb cuts that will no longer be utilized shall be closed.

Any discontinuances (sub-surface, surface or above surface) within the Public ROW must be processed through

Easements:
Any easements within the Public ROW associated with this project must be processed through the PIC.
Landscaping:
The developer must seek approval from the Chief Landscape Architect with the Parks and Recreation Department
for all landscape elements within the Public ROW. The landscaping program must accompany a LM&I with the
PIC.
Street Lighting:
The developer must seek approval from the PWD Street Lighting Division, where needed, for all proposed street
lighting to be installed by the developer. All proposed lighting within the Public ROW must be compatible with the
area lighting to provide a consistent urban design. The developer should coordinate with the PWD Street Lighting
Division for an assessment of any additional street lighting upgrades that are to be considered in conjunction with
this project. All existing metal street light pull box covers within the limits of sidewalk construction to remain shall be
replaced with new composite covers per PWD Street Lighting standards. Metal covers should remain for pull box
covers in the roadway. For all sections of sidewalk that are to be reconstructed in the Public ROW that contain or
are proposed to contain a City-owned street light system with underground conduit, the developer shall be
responsible for installing shadow conduit adjacent to the street lighting system. Installation of shadow conduit and
limits should be coordinated through the BPDA Smart Utilities team.
Roadway:
Based on the extent of construction activity, including utility connections and taps, the developer will be responsible
for the full restoration of the roadway sections that immediately abut the property and, in some cases, to extend the
limits of roadway restoration to the nearest intersection. A plan showing the extents and methods for roadway
restoration shall be submitted to the PWD Engineering Division for review and approval.
Additional Project Coordination:
All projects must be entered into the City of Boston Utility Coordination Software (COBUCS) to review for any
conflicts with other proposed projects within the Public ROW. The developer must coordinate with any existing
projects within the same limits and receive clearance from PWD before commencing work.
Green Infrastructure:
The developer shall work with PWD, the Green Infrastructure Division, and the Boston Water and Sewer
Commission (BWSC) to determine appropriate methods of green infrastructure and/or stormwater management
systems within the Public ROW. The ongoing maintenance of such systems shall require an LM&I Agreement with
the PIC. Effects of water infiltration with respect to the adjacent underpass structure and underground MBTA
tunnels that may be negatively impacted by infiltration may impact the ability to install such systems and should be
considered. Coordination with PWD and MBTA will be required.
Resiliency:
Proposed designs should follow the Boston Public Works Climate Resilient Design Guidelines
(https://www.boston.gov/environment-and-energy/climate-resilient-design-guidelines) where applicable.

INTRODUCTION 
 
The Boston College (the “University”) Institutional Master Plan (“IMP”) was approved 
by the Boston Redevelopment Authority (“BRA”) Board in 2009, was renewed in 
2013 and 2017 for four-year periods, and was renewed again in 2021 and 2023 for 
two-year periods. On July 12, 2023, the University submitted a Fifth Amendment to 
the Boston College Institutional Master Plan (the “Fifth IMP Amendment”). The 
proposed Fifth Amendment reflects modifications to the Library Storage Project, 
which, as amended, will be the Catholic Religious Archive (the “Proposed Project”). 
 
PROJECT SITE 
 
The Project Site is located in the western portion of the University’s 66-acre 
Brighton Campus. It is buffered from the residential neighborhood by intervening 
topography and wooded area. Access to the Project Site is from the Brighton 
Campus “Spine Road,” which is located off Commonwealth Avenue, a major arterial 
roadway. 
 
The Project is located on the interior of the University’s Brighton Campus, to the 
west of the “Spine Road,” in the Brighton neighborhood of Boston, Massachusetts. 
The Project Site is bordered land along Lake Street to the west, the Lake Street 
entrance to the Brighton Campus to the north, the “Spine Road” to the east, and the 
Library to the south.

DESCRIPTION OF THE FIFTH AMENDMENT TO THE BC IMP 
 
Originally described in the 2009 Boston College IMP as an approximately 14,000 
square foot addition to the Theological and Ministry Library, the Fifth Amendment 
to the BC IMP seeks to change the originally described project to an approximately 
45,000 square foot building attached to the Theological and Ministry Library. No 
other changes are contemplated. 
 
PROPOSED PROJECT 
 
The Library Storage Project, originally described in the 2009 IMP as an 
approximately 40-foot high, 14,000 square foot addition to the Theology and 
Ministry Library on the Brighton Campus. The Library Storage Project was located 
immediately to the North of the Library and east of Lake Street (the “Project Site”). 
 
The amended Library Storage Project, referred to as the Catholic Religious Archives 
Project, will be in the same location as the Library Storage project, but enlarged to 
comprise less than 45,000 sf Gross Floor Area (“GFA”) with an overall height less 
than 55 feet.

When complete, the Project will primarily store collections, as well as limited 
artwork and cultural artifacts. The two floors of the building will have a mixture of 
fixed and compact shelving, map cases, and art racks. The consistent internal 
climate of the collection and processing spaces will be serviced from climate control 
mechanical equipment in a partial basement. The building will have a loading dock, 
internal receiving area, and a holding room for collection of objects. The Project will 
utilize space in the Library for processing and a research reading room that will be 
accessed by a one-story connector between the two buildings. 
 
Transportation access for the building’s visitors and staff in accordance with the 
University’s overall parking and transportation plan, which includes a campus 
shuttle serving the Brighton Campus with a stop at Commonwealth Avenue at 
Greycliff Road. Sufficient parking is available to meet anticipated demand in the 
existing surface parking lots located directly east of the Library. The Project will also 
incorporate two service parking spaces along the building and two accessible 
parking spaces to the west of the building.

ARTICLE 80 AND PUBLIC REVIEW 
 
The IMPNF for Amendment, filed on July 12, 2024, is being reviewed under the 
Expedited Review Procedure of Section 80D-9.2 of the Code. Pursuant to Section 
80D-9.2 of the Code, a proposed amendment to an IMP may be submitted under an 
expedited review procedure if: (1) such amendment proposes no changes to the 
IMP other that the addition of one of more Proposed Projects; and (2) each of such 
Proposed Projects meets the requirements of Section 80D-9.2(b) (i) or (ii) and does 
not meet the size thresholds of Large Project Review. The Proposed Project does 
not meet the threshold for Large Project Review and complies with the 
requirements of 80D-9.2(b)(ii). No other changes are proposed. There was a joint, 
BC Task Force and public meeting on August 6, 2024. The comment period for the 
IMPNF closed on August 11, 2024. 
 
Planning and Zoning Context 
 
Boston College seeks to build a new Catholic archives facility, as an addition to an 
existing theology library. The Proposed Project is located in the Brighton Campus of 
the school, governed by Boston College Institutional Master Plan (IMP) zoning. The

existing IMP was approved by the BRA in 2009. In 2013 the IMP was renewed for 
four years, and then again was renewed in 2017 for four years. In 2021 it was 
renewed for two years, and most recently in 2023 it was renewed for another two 
year period through October 14, 2025. 
 
The existing IMP identifies the location of the Proposed Project as a site for future 
library storage. Staff have determined that the proposed use is well aligned with 
the intended use described by the site’s existing IMP zoning. The existing IMP 
describes the storage facility on this site as a 40 foot, 14,000 square foot addition to 
an existing library. The Proposed Project’s dimensions have increased to 55 feet 
and 44,000 square feet. The proposed dimensions would facilitate new storage 
demands of the library and achieve program goals of the school outlined in the 
purpose of the IMP, while having minimal impact on the surrounding context. 
 
Parking requirements will be satisfied by two accessible parking spaces, two service 
parking spaces and a loading area in front of the entrance to the Proposed Project.

documents that the Director deems appropriate and necessary in connection with

INTRODUCTION 
 
The Boston College (the “University”) Institutional Master Plan (“IMP”) was approved 
by the Boston Redevelopment Authority (“BRA”) Board in 2009, was renewed in 
2013 and 2017 for four-year periods, and was renewed again in 2021 and 2023 for 
two-year periods. On July 12, 2023, the University submitted a Fifth Amendment to 
the Boston College Institutional Master Plan (the “Fifth IMP Amendment”). The 
proposed Fifth Amendment reflects modifications to the Library Storage Project, 
which, as amended, will be the Catholic Religious Archive (the “Proposed Project”). 
 
PROJECT SITE 
 
The Project Site is located in the western portion of the University’s 66-acre 
Brighton Campus. It is buffered from the residential neighborhood by intervening 
topography and wooded area. Access to the Project Site is from the Brighton 
Campus “Spine Road,” which is located off Commonwealth Avenue, a major arterial 
roadway. 
 
The Project is located on the interior of the University’s Brighton Campus, to the 
west of the “Spine Road,” in the Brighton neighborhood of Boston, Massachusetts. 
The Project Site is bordered land along Lake Street to the west, the Lake Street 
entrance to the Brighton Campus to the north, the “Spine Road” to the east, and the 
Library to the south.

DESCRIPTION OF THE FIFTH AMENDMENT TO THE BC IMP 
 
Originally described in the 2009 Boston College IMP as an approximately 14,000 
square foot addition to the Theological and Ministry Library, the Fifth Amendment 
to the BC IMP seeks to change the originally described project to an approximately 
45,000 square foot building attached to the Theological and Ministry Library. No 
other changes are contemplated. 
 
PROPOSED PROJECT 
 
The Library Storage Project, originally described in the 2009 IMP as an 
approximately 40-foot high, 14,000 square foot addition to the Theology and 
Ministry Library on the Brighton Campus. The Library Storage Project was located 
immediately to the North of the Library and east of Lake Street (the “Project Site”). 
 
The amended Library Storage Project, referred to as the Catholic Religious Archives 
Project, will be in the same location as the Library Storage project, but enlarged to 
comprise less than 45,000 sf Gross Floor Area (“GFA”) with an overall height less 
than 55 feet.

When complete, the Project will primarily store collections, as well as limited 
artwork and cultural artifacts. The two floors of the building will have a mixture of 
fixed and compact shelving, map cases, and art racks. The consistent internal 
climate of the collection and processing spaces will be serviced from climate control 
mechanical equipment in a partial basement. The building will have a loading dock, 
internal receiving area, and a holding room for collection of objects. The Project will 
utilize space in the Library for processing and a research reading room that will be 
accessed by a one-story connector between the two buildings. 
 
Transportation access for the building’s visitors and staff in accordance with the 
University’s overall parking and transportation plan, which includes a campus 
shuttle serving the Brighton Campus with a stop at Commonwealth Avenue at 
Greycliff Road. Sufficient parking is available to meet anticipated demand in the 
existing surface parking lots located directly east of the Library. The Project will also 
incorporate two service parking spaces along the building and two accessible 
parking spaces to the west of the building.

The IMPNF for Amendment, filed on July 12, 2024, is being reviewed under the 
Expedited Review Procedure of Section 80D-9.2 of the Code. Pursuant to Section 
80D-9.2 of the Code, a proposed amendment to an IMP may be submitted under an 
expedited review procedure if: (1) such amendment proposes no changes to the 
IMP other that the addition of one of more Proposed Projects; and (2) each of such 
Proposed Projects meets the requirements of Section 80D-9.2(b) (i) or (ii) and does 
not meet the size thresholds of Large Project Review. The Proposed Project does 
not meet the threshold for Large Project Review and complies with the 
requirements of 80D-9.2(b)(ii). No other changes are proposed. There was a joint, 
BC Task Force and public meeting on August 6, 2024. The comment period for the 
IMPNF closed on August 11, 2024. 
 
Planning and Zoning Context 
 
Boston College seeks to build a new Catholic archives facility, as an addition to an 
existing theology library. The Proposed Project is located in the Brighton Campus of 
the school, governed by Boston College Institutional Master Plan (IMP) zoning. The 
----1
