TO: 
BOSTON REDEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY 
D/B/A BOSTON PLANNING & DEVELOPMENT AGENCY (BPDA) 
AND KAIROS SHEN, DIRECTOR 
FROM: 
CASEY HINES, SR. DEPUTY DIRECTOR OF DEVELOPMENT REVIEW 
NUPOOR MONANI, SR. DEP. DIRECTOR OF DEVELOPMENT REVIEW 
SARAH PECK, DEVELOPMENT PORTFOLIO MANAGER 
SUBJECT: 
ONE MYSTIC AVENUE, CHARLESTOWN – NOTICE OF PROJECT 
CHANGE 
 
 
SUMMARY: 
 
This Memorandum requests that the Boston Redevelopment 
Authority (“BRA”) d/b/a Boston Planning & Development Agency 
(“BPDA”) authorize the Director to: (1) issue a Determination 
waiving further review of the One Mystic Avenue Project (the 
“Proposed Project”), pursuant to Section 80A-6.1 of the City of 
Boston Zoning Code (the “Code”) in connection with the Notice of 
Project Change (the “NPC”) filed by Fulcrum Global Investors on 
August 8, 2025; (2) issue a Certification of Compliance for the 
Proposed Project pursuant to Section 80B-6 of the Code, upon 
successful completion of the Article 80 Large Project Review 
Process; and (3) enter into an Affordable Rental Housing 
Agreement and Restriction, an Affordable Contribution Agreement, 
and any and all other documents that the Director deems 
appropriate and necessary and containing terms and conditions 
determined by the Director to be in the best interest of the BRA, in 
connection with the Proposed Project. 
 
 
PROJECT SITE 
The project site consists of approximately 60,089 square feet (approximately 1.4 
acres) of land known and numbered as 1 Mystic Avenue and bounded generally by 
Sherman Street to the west, the 3 Sherman Street lot and Temple Street (a private 
way) to the north, Dorrance Street to the East, and Mystic Avenue to the south (the 
“Project Site”). The Project Site is currently occupied by a 4,800-square-foot 

 
BOARD APPROVED 
26 
 
2 
 
residential/commercial building previously occupied partially by Flynn’s Auto 
Salvage (located at 1-3 Mystic Avenue), a vacant 8,600-square-foot commercial 
building, a plumbing and refrigeration business (located at 3 Sherman Street), a 
transformer building, a cell tower, and associated parking and access drives. 
DEVELOPMENT TEAM 
The Development Team for the Proposed Project consists of: 
Proponent/Applicant: 
One Mystic Owner, LLC 
Affiliate of Fulcrum Global Investors, LLC 
Scott D. Brown, CFA 
John Brainard 
Kurt Hunziker

Legal Counsel:

Donald Wiest 
Michael W. Parker 
 
Community Engagement 
& Government Relations: 
KRM Consulting Services 
Kimberly Mahoney

Transportation Engineer 
& Permitting Consultant: 
VHB 
Selma Mandzo-Preldzic, P.E. 
Stephanie Kruel, ENV SP 
 
 
BACKGROUND 
On September 28, 2023, the BPDA Board approved the Proposed Project, which 
consists of a development project of an up to 280-foot-high, 22-story multifamily 
residential building containing (i) approximately Five-Hundred and Three (503) 

 
BOARD APPROVED 
26 
 
3 
 
dwelling units; (ii) ground-floor retail/restaurant and community space; (iii) 
accessory below-grade parking for up to One-Hundred and Eleven (111) cars; and 
(iv) other typical supporting uses and facilities for a multifamily residential 
apartment project. In total, the Project will include up to 360,534 square feet of 
gross floor area, including approximately 8,900 square feet of supporting ground-
floor lobby, retail / service / restaurant space and shared-use amenity space 
distributed throughout the building. 
The Boston Zoning Commission has approved the Development Plan for Planned 
Development Area (PDA) No. 143, located at 1 Mystic Avenue, Charlestown, dated 
June 12, 2023. The approval includes an amendment to Zoning Map 2B/2C 
(Charlestown Waterfront) by designating the site as a Planned Development Area 
(PDA Overlay District). This designation applies to approximately 60,089 square feet 
(1.4 acres) of land bounded by Sherman Street, Temple Street, Dorrance Street, and 
Mystic Avenue. 
The Project has been studied in connection with the comprehensive planning 
initiative known as PLAN: Charlestown. The proposed Project is consistent with the 
final PLAN: Charlestown recommendations for this location. 
NOTICE OF PROJECT CHANGE 
Since receiving BPDA Board and Zoning Commission approvals in 2023, economic 
conditions and housing demand have shifted significantly. In response to these 
changes, the Proponent is seeking to amend the approved rental program to 
include a portion of the building as condominium homeownership opportunities. 
Updates include: 
• Reduction of height from 22 to 18 stories 
• Reduction of total units from 503 to 423 
o 221 for-sale condominium units 
o 202 for-rent apartment units 
• Reduction of 111 on-site parking spaces 
• Internal EV car share program with 5 vehicles 
• Reduction in building footprint, increasing open space and street frontage 
 
All design changes described above, including the height, parking, and building 
footprint, are allowed as of right under the approved Development Plan for PDA 
No. 143. The residential rental units include approximately one-hundred twelve 

 
BOARD APPROVED 
26 
 
4 
 
(112) studio units, sixty-seven (67) one-bedroom units, seventeen (17) two-bedroom 
units, and six (6) three-bedroom units, all of which are compact units. The 
residential homeownership units include approximately one-hundred six (106) 
studio units and one-hundred fifteen (115) one-bedroom units.

AFFIRMATIVELY FURTHERING FAIR HOUSING 
 
The Proposed Project incorporates the following Affirmatively Furthering Fair 
Housing Interventions: 
 
Article 80 Interventions: 
• Provide more IDP units than are required under the IDP policy; 
• Increase building density to directly increase affordable units for and 
available to protected classes; and 
• Provide a greater number of Group 2 units than required. 
 
Marketing & Housing Access Interventions: 
• Provide a preference for an agreed upon percentage of units to rental 
voucher-holders for the first year or some other term; 
• Allow last month’s rent and security deposit to be paid in installments for an 
agreed upon percentage of units or by renters up to a certain income level; 
• Agree to follow best practices related to the use of CORI, eviction, and credit 
records in the tenant screening and selection process; and 
• Agree to best practices in marketing the market-rate units that are inclusive 
of and welcoming to protected classes. 
 
INCLUSIONARY DEVELOPMENT POLICY 
The Proposed Project is subject to the Inclusionary Development Policy, dated 
December 10, 2015 (“IDP”), and is located within Zone B, as defined by the IDP 
which requires that 13% of total residential units be provided as on-site IDP units, 
or off-site units, or payment in lieu of units for 18% of market-rate units. In this 
case, the Proposed Project seeks authorization to move forward with either of two 
affordability proposals for the rental component of the project, as further detailed 
herein (“Option 1” and “Option 2”), which will be memorialized in an Affordable 
Housing Agreement and Restriction (“ARHAR”), and a payment in lieu of units for 
the homeownership component of the project, which will be memorialized in an 
Affordable Housing Contribution Agreement (“AHCA”).

units, of which twenty-seven (27) units (the “IDP Units”), or approximately 13% of

(“AMI”), as published annually by the BPDA and based on upon data from the 
United States Department of Housing and Urban Development (“HUD”), as well as 
approximately fourteen (14) units (the “VASH Units”) made available to veterans 
with housing vouchers under the Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing program 
(VASH).

In either Options 1 or 2, the location of the IDP Units and VASH Units (where 
applicable) will be finalized in conjunction with BPDA and Mayor’s Office of Housing 
(“MOH”) staff and outlined in the ARHAR, and rental prices and income limits for the 
IDP Units will be adjusted according to BPDA published maximum rental prices and 
income limits, as based on HUD AMIs, available at the time of the initial rental of 
the IDP Units, and the rental prices and income limits for the VASH Units will be 
adjusted according to the MOH published Small Area Fair Market Rent (“SAFMR”) for 
Charlestown zip code 02129, as based on data from the Boston Housing Authority, 
available at the time of the initial rental of the VASH Units (where applicable). IDP 
Units must be comparable in size, design, and quality to the market-rate units in 
the Proposed Project, cannot be stacked or concentrated on the same floors, and 
must be consistent in bedroom count with the entire Proposed Project, and the 
VASH Units will be collocated within an area of the rental component of the 
Proposed Project for proximity to relevant amenity and services space for use of 
the tenants of the VASH Units. 
 
If the proponent receives a building permit for the Proposed Project on or before 
March 18, 2027, 18 months from the approval date of this Board Memorandum, the 
homeownership component of the Proposed Project will make a payment in lieu of 
approximately 39.78 homeownership units, or approximately 18% of total 
homeownership units within the project, at a value determined as the greater of 
either the Zone Factor for Zone B ($300,000 per unit) or half the difference between 
the average market price and the affordable price per unit, by unit type. 
 
In this case, the payment shall be approximately Eighteen Million One-Hundred 
Twenty-Six Thousand Nine-Hundred Seventy-Five and 02/100 Dollars 
($18,126,975.02), and made in the four (4) installments detailed below: 
 

 
BOARD APPROVED 
26 
 
11 
 
1. Twelve (12) months after the issuance of COO for the Proposed Project, the 
Proponent shall make a payment into the IDP Fund of an amount prorated to 
18% of total homeownership units sold within the project prior to the date of 
this first invoice, at a value determined as the greater of either the Zone 
Factor for Zone B ($300,000 per unit) or half the difference between the 
average market price and the affordable price per unit, by unit type, 
excluding all unsold units; and 
2. Twenty-four (24) months after the issuance of COO for the Proposed Project, 
the Proponent shall make a payment into the IDP Fund of an amount 
prorated to 18% of total homeownership units sold within the project prior 
to the date of this second invoice, excluding all units accounted for in the first 
installment paid for the first invoice, at a value determined as the greater of 
either the Zone Factor for Zone B ($300,000 per unit) or half the difference 
between the average market price and the affordable price per unit, by unit 
type, excluding all unsold units; and 
3. Thirty-six (36) months after the issuance of COO for the Proposed Project, 
the Proponent shall make a payment into the IDP Fund of an amount 
prorated to 18% of total homeownership units sold within the project prior 
to the date of this third invoice, excluding all units accounted for in the first 
and second installments paid for the first and second invoices, at a value 
determined as the greater of either the Zone Factor for Zone B ($300,000 per 
unit) or half the difference between the average market price and the 
affordable price per unit, by unit type, excluding all unsold units; and 
4. Forty-eight (48) months after the issuance of COO for the Proposed Project, 
the Proponent shall make a payment into the IDP Fund of an amount 
prorated to 18% of total homeownership units sold within the project prior 
to the date of this fourth invoice as well as 18% of total unsold 
homeownership units in the project, excluding all units accounted for in the 
first, second, and third installments paid for the first, second, and third 
invoices, at a value determined as the greater of either the Zone Factor for 
Zone B ($300,000 per unit) or half the difference between the average market 
price and the affordable price per unit, by unit type, using the advertised 
prices for all unsold units. 

 
BOARD APPROVED 
26 
 
12 
 
Absent force majeure, if the Proponent does not receive a building permit for the 
Proposed Project on or before March 18, 2027, 18 months from the approval date 
of this Board Memorandum, the Proponent shall restrict units in a manner 
consistent with the IDP commitment of the PDA, which is a minimum 10% of total 
homeownership units at 80% AMI and 10% of total homeownership units at 100% 
AMI. Such period may be extended by the BPDA, in cooperation with MOH, for a 
maximum period of 24 months. 
The ARHAR and AHCA must be executed prior to the issuance of the Certification of 
Compliance for the Proposed Project. The Proponent must also register the 
Proposed Project with the Boston Fair Housing Commission (“BFHC”) upon issuance 
of the building permit. The IDP Units and VASH Units (where applicable) will not be 
marketed prior to the submission and approval of an Affirmative Marketing Plan to 
the BFHC and the BPDA. Preference will be given to applicants who meet the 
following criteria, weighted in the order below: 
1. Boston resident; and 
2. Household size (a minimum of one (1) person per bedroom). 
 
Where a unit is built out for a specific disability (e.g., mobility or sensory), a 
preference will also be available to households with a person whose need matches 
the build out of the unit. The City of Boston Disabilities Commission may assist the 
BPDA in determining eligibility for such a preference. 
 
An affordability covenant will be placed on the IDP Units and VASH Units (where 
applicable) to maintain affordability for a total period of fifty (50) years (this 
includes thirty (30) years with an option to extend for an additional period of twenty 
(20) years). The household income of the renter and the rent of any subsequent 
rental of the IDP Units and VASH Units (where applicable) during this fifty (50) year 
period must fall within the applicable income and rent limits for each IDP Unit and 
VASH Units (where applicable). IDP Units and VASH Units (where applicable) may 
not be rented out by the developer prior to rental to an income eligible household, 
and the BPDA or its assigns or successors will monitor the ongoing affordability of 
the IDP Units and VASH Units (where applicable). 
 
RECOMMENDATION 
It is the staff recommendation that the BPDA approve the changes to the Proposed 
Project and authorize the Director to: (1) issue a Determination waiving further 
review pursuant to Section 80A-6.1 of the Code in connection with the NPC filed by 

 
BOARD APPROVED 
26 
 
13 
 
Fulcrum Global Investors on August 8, 2025; (2) issue a Certification of Compliance, 
pursuant to Section 80B-6 of the Code, upon successful completion of the Article 80 
Large Project Review Process; and (3) enter into an Affordable Rental Housing 
Agreement and Restriction, an Affordable Housing Contribution Agreement, and 
any and all other documents that the Director deems appropriate and necessary 
and containing terms and conditions determined by the Director to be in the best 
interest of the BRA, in connection with the NPC. 
 
An appropriate vote follows: 
VOTED: 
That the Director be, and hereby is, authorized to issue a 
Determination waiving further review pursuant to Section 80A-6.1 of 
the Boston Zoning Code (the “Code”), which finds that the Notice of 
Project Change submitted by Fulcrum Global Investors (the 
"Proponent"), to the Boston Redevelopment Authority (the “BRA”) on 
August 8, 2025, does not significantly increase the impact of the One 
Mystic Avenue Project (the “Proposed Project”), and that no further 
review of the Proposed Project is required, subject to continuing 
design review by the BRA; and 
 
FURTHER 
VOTED: 
That the Director be, and hereby is, authorized to issue a Certification 
of Compliance for the Proposed Project, pursuant to Section 
80B-6 of the Code, upon successful completion of the Article 80 Large 
Project Review Process; 
 
FURTHER 
VOTED: 
That the Director be, and hereby is, authorized to execute and deliver 
an Affordable Rental Housing Agreement and Restriction in connection 
with forty-one (41) on-site income-restricted units, an Affordable 
Housing Contribution Agreement in connection with a payment in lieu 
of 18% of homeownership units, and any and all agreements and 
documents which the Director deems appropriate and necessary in 
connection with the Proposed Project, all upon terms and conditions 
determined to be in the best interests of the Boston Redevelopment 
Authority.

PROJECT SITE 
 
The project site is comprised of two (2) former MBTA-owned parcels, the first 
bounded by Tremont, Gurney, and Station Streets, an MBTA pumping station and 
the MBTA tracks/Southwest Corridor, and a second smaller parcel located on the 
Northeast corner of Gurney Street in Mission Hill. The larger parcel known as Parcel 
25 contained approximately 76,703 square feet (1.76 acres) and the smaller parcel, 
known as Parcel 25B, contained approximately 5,500 square feet for a total of 
approximately 82,203 square feet of land area (“PDA area”). The Proposed Project 
will be developed on the subdivided Parcel 25H which consists of approximately 
32,144 square feet of vacant land, currently used for construction staging for Phase 
2 of the Parcel 25 Project (“Phase 2”) and surface parking for Phase 1A of the Parcel 
25 project (“Phase 1A”).

DESCRIPTION AND PROGRAM 
 
The Proposed Project will redevelop the under-utilized Parcel 25H site within the 
PDA Area with construction of a new six (6) story, approximately 120,000 GSF 
building with up to ninety-four (94) affordable rental units and 33 above ground 
parking spaces, including eight (8) for the sole use of the Proposed Project residents 
and the remaining 25 spaces as ancillary parking for the adjacent Phase 1A Project, 
including residential, office and retail spaces. 
 
In light of the changing real estate market and continually increasing construction 
costs since the original project approvals, the Proposed Project amends the original 
Phase 3 Project, which consisted of approximately 161,500 gross square feet of 
commercial office space in a much taller and larger building. The original Phase 3 
building was anticipated to be 160 feet tall and included 185 spaces in below 
ground parking plates. However, given the City of Boston changes from minimum 
parking allowances to maximum parking allowance and the parking change in 
zoning for affordable housing projects, the Proponent is modifying the residential 
parking allowance with the Proposed Project. As such, the Proposed Project is a 
significant reduction in height, density, and use of this phase of the Development 
Plan for Planned Development Area No. 100, Parcel 25/Parcel 25B, Mission Hill 
Neighborhood (the “Development Plan”).

PLANNING CONTEXT 
 
This Proposed Project is located in the Roxbury Crossing area of Mission Hill. The 
site is in a walkable area, well served by transit and local retail amenities. The 
Roxbury Crossing MBTA Orange Line station and stops for the 18 and 22 MBTA bus 
routes are located across the street from the site. The area is characterized by a 
mix of active ground floor uses, housing, public open space, and institutional uses. 
While this particular phase provides minimal open space, taken in the context of 
the full PDA area, the Proposed Project provides appropriate public open space. 
 
The site is governed by PDA No. 100, which is based upon a community-based 
visioning exercise undertaken to inform the reuse of this former MBTA surplus 
parcel. The proposed NPC falls within the dimensional framework of the original 
PDA. Proposed dimensional changes are appropriate, and a function of the shift in 
proposed use from office to residential. 
 
The Proposed Project is located within the MBTA’s Zone of Influence (ZOI). The 
MBTA requires that the development team obtain an MBTA license prior to entering 
and/or performing any work on or over MBTA property or within the MBTA’s ZOI. 
 
 
ZONING 
 
The PDA Area is located within the Mission Hill Neighborhood District and is located 
within the Roxbury Crossing Community Commercial Subdistrict (“CC-2”). The CC-2 
Subdistrict allows for a Maximum Building Height of 160 feet and a Maximum Floor 
Area Ratio (“FAR”) of 5.0 in a PDA pursuant to Article 59-30 of the Code. The NPC 
Proposed Project as proposed and added to the previously constructed phases 

 
6 
brings the full build out of all three (3) phases to an FAR of approximately 3.06, 
which will not exceed the allowable PDA Maximum Building Height of 160 feet. In 
addition, the CC-2 Subdistrict requires no Minimum Lot Size, Minimum Lot Width, 
Minimum Lot Frontage, Minimum Front Yard, Minimum Side yard, or Useable Open 
Space per Dwelling Unit. As such, the Proposed Project is designed to comply with 
the standards and requirements set forth in Article 59 of the Code applicable to 
PDAs. 
 
Furthermore, the Proposed Project is an all-affordable development project, and as 
such, no off-street parking is required pursuant to Zoning Text Amendment No. 454 
dated December 22, 2021, which states that: “in case of affordable residential 
housing, no off-street parking shall be required. Affordable residential housing shall 
be considered to describe those projects where at least 60% of the proposed 
residential units are income-restricted at or below 100% of Area Median Income 
(AMI), as defined by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.” 
 
MITIGATION & COMMUNITY BENEFITS 
 
The Proposed Project will provide substantial public benefits for the City and its 
residents in both the short-term and the long-term. These benefits include the 
following: 
 
● Completes the revitalization of Roxbury Crossing as a gateway to the 
Mission Hill neighborhood; 
● Creates up to ninety-four (94) units of affordable residential rental 
housing units; 
● Introduces new neighborhood residents who will provide support to 
the local community and utilize local businesses; 
● Activates an underutilized site, replaces a 32,144 square foot vacant 
lot, and contributes to the future growth and stability of Roxbury 
Crossing; 
● Offers an opportunity for a transit-oriented location within walking 
distance of the Roxbury Crossing Orange Line Station, steps away from 
the MBTA bus stop with numerous bus routes along Tremont Street as 
well and the SW Corridor Park and bike path; 
● Continues a thoughtfully designed streetscape that improves and 
enhances the pedestrian landscape and experience at its completed 
pedestrian pathway that serves as public open space and street edges 
through its use of natural vegetation and architectural elements; 

 
7 
● The NPC Project will be designed and constructed to meet the USGBC’s 
LEED v4 BD+C Multifamily Midrise Gold standard by achieving 72+ 
points. 
● In alignment with the city’s carbon neutral goals, the NPC project is 
designed to target 2035 pCEI value of 1.17 kg CO2e/sf-yr prioritizing 
high performance building enclosure solutions that meet Passive 
House standards. 
● The project will be designed with all-efficient electric systems for 
heating, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC) and energy star-rated 
equipment. The team will assess the feasibility of air source heat 
pumps (ASHP) for Domestic hot water (DHW) needs and as a minimum 
the project will be ready for future hot water electrification on 
construction completion. 
● The design will be optimized for solar renewable energy output with a 
minimum 102+ kW array size modeled for the rooftop of Ph 3 building. 
Modeled system locations and sizes will be finalized prior to Article 37 
approval with a goal on onsite installation during construction. 
● The project team will also work to determine what utility incentives are 
available for electrification, procurement of 100% renewable electricity 
for common areas and tenant loads and opportunities to reduce 
embodied carbon through material studies. 
● Temporarily creates many new jobs in the construction and building 
trade industries; 
● Adds new annual property taxes for the City of Boston; and 
● Includes ninety-four (94) bicycle parking spaces. 
● The Proposed Project will provide space for one 15-dock bike share 
station onsite upon issuance of Certificate of Occupancy. The 
proponent will work with BTD and the BPDA to site the station 
appropriately. Bike share stations may require Administrative Review 
by PIC. 
● The Proponent will design and implement accessible pedestrian ramps 
connecting the project site across Station Street to Mindoro Street. 
This mitigation measure is subject to BPDA, BTD, PWD, and other city 
or state agency review as needed. PIC approvals for proposed 
improvements shall be completed before building permit issuance for 
the Proposed Project. The physical mitigation improvements must be 
completed upon Certificate of Occupancy. 
 
AFFIRMATIVELY FURTHERING FAIR HOUSING (“AFFH”)

The Proposed Project has agreed to the following AFFH interventions: 
 
Article 80 Interventions: 
● Provide an additional percentage of income-restricted units (100% of units) 
than required by the IDP; 
● Deepen the affordability of IDP units, with units offered at 30%, 50%, 60% 
and 70% of AMI; 
● Provide all affordable units on-site; 
● Provide higher proportion of family-sized income-restricted units than 
required: 74% of the 94 units will have two or more (2+) bedrooms; 
● Increase the number of fully built-out Group 2 units accessible to persons 
with disabilities, and exceed accessibility requirements by voluntarily 
proposing to provide 15 Units (16%) as Group 2 units, including nine (9) 
Group 2B fully accessible units and an additional six (6) Group 2A fully 
adaptable units. Included in the nine (9) Group 2B units are three (3) CBH 
units with additional accessibility features; 
● Increase building density to directly increase affordable units for and 
available to people in protected classes; 
● Agree to apply to host Project Based Vouchers or Rental Assistance 
Demonstration units onsite, in addition to meeting and exceeding 
affordability requirements of the IDP. The Proponent is applying for nineteen 
(19) units within the Proposed Project to be able to receive project-based 
vouchers (including eight (8) project-based Section-8 units, eight (8) project-
based MRVP units, and three (3) Section 811 units). Families with mobile 
housing vouchers will be welcome to all other units within the Proposed 
Project; 
● Partner with a non-profit developer, land trust, housing authority, or other 
entity to provide land or bear some capital costs to enable affordable 
housing construction, in addition to fulfilling IDP requirements, namely, 
Mission Hill Neighborhood Housing Services (MHNHS), a non-profit 
developer. 
 
Marketing and Access Interventions: 
● Provide a preference for an agreed upon percentage of units to rental 
voucher-holders and develop marketing and tenant selection policies and 
procedures that are least likely to exclude voucher-holders; 
● Agree to follow best practices related to the use of CORI, eviction, and credit 
records in the tenant screening and selection process;

● Agree to follow progressive practices related to the use of CORI, eviction, and 
credit records in the tenant screening and selection process, and in 
marketing of units, for example following Fair Chance Housing guidelines, 
and/or waiving eviction and credit checks for affordable units and/or housing 
voucher-holders. 
 
The Proponent must submit to the Boston Interagency Fair Housing Development

HOUSING PROGRAM AND INCLUSIONARY DEVELOPMENTPOLICY 
COMMITMENTS 
 
Projects financed as one entity and where at least 40% of the units are income 
restricted are exempt from the Inclusionary Development Policy (the “IDP”), dated 
December 10, 2015. The Proposed Project is financed as one entity and contains up 
to ninety-four (94) income restricted rental units, or approximately 100% of the 
total units, surpassing 40% of the total units. As such, the Proposed Project is 
exempt from the IDP. 
 
Of the ninety-four (94) rental units within the Proposed Project, twenty-four (24) 
units will be one-bedroom units, fifty-five (55) units will be two-bedroom units, and 
the remaining fifteen (15) units will be three-bedroom units. 
 
Of the 94 total units, nineteen (19) will be made affordable to households earning 
not more than 30% of the Area Median Income (“AMI”), as determined by the 
Department of Housing and Urban Development (“HUD”), ten (10) will be made 
affordable to households earning not more than 50% AMI, forty-two (42) units will 
be affordable to households earning not more than 60% AMI, and the remaining 
twenty-three (23) units will be identified as Workforce units and made affordable to 
households earning not more than 70% AMI. 
 
The affordability of the Proposed Project will be finalized through the public 
funding process and the ongoing affordability of the project will be monitored 
under a MassDocs agreement.

First Amendment Proposed 
Improvements for NPC Phase 3 
Project 
The NPC Parcel 25 Phase 3 project will revitalize this final 
under-utilized site with construction of a new six (6) story, 
approximately 120,000 gsf building with up to 94 affordable 
rental residences and 33 above ground parking spaces, 
including eight (8) for the sole use of NPC Phase 3 Project 
residents and the remaining 25 spaces will be ancillary 
parking for the adjacent Parcel 25 Phase 1A project, 
including residential, office and retail spaces.

additional affordable rental housing in the Mission Hill 
neighborhood, which the Proponent submits has been clearly 
demonstrated by the 3,100 applicants for the most recent 46-
units at the Parcel 25 Phase 2 Project. In light of the

construction costs since the original project approvals, the

gross square feet of commercial office space in a much taller 
and larger building. The original Phase 3 building was

modifying the residential parking allowance with the NPC

reduction in height, density and use of this phase of the PDA

Proposed Uses 
The NPC Phase 3 Project now contains up to 94 units of

The Original Plan encompassed approximately 1.89 acres of land in the Mission Hill 
neighborhood of Boston at Tremont and Gurney Streets, as described in Exhibit A to the Original 
Plan. It is comprised of two (2) former MBTA-owned parcels, the first bounded by Tremont, Gurney, 
and Station Streets, an MBTA pumping station and the MBTA tracks/Southwest Corridor (“Parcel 
25”), and a second smaller parcel located on the northeast corner of Gurney Street in Mission Hill 
(“Parcel 25B”). The larger parcel known as Parcel 25 contained approximately 76,703 square feet 
and the smaller parcel, known as Parcel 25B, contained approximately 5,500 square feet for a total of 
approximately 82,203 square feet of land area (collectively, the “PDA Area”). There are no proposed 
changes to the Site or PDA Area as part of the First Amendment. 
 
The Original Plan provided for development of a mixed-use residential, retail, and 
commercial development of up to 305,750 gross square feet to be developed in multiple phases: Phase 
1 to consist of two (2) buildings – Building 1A of approximately 76,250 gross square feet and 
Building 1B of approximately 12,000 gross square feet; Phase 2 of approximately 56,000 gross square 
feet in Building 2; and Phase 3 of approximately 161,500 gross square feet in Building 3 (collectively, 
the “Project”). 
 
Under the Original Plan, the Building 1B of Phase 1 (the “Building 1B”) was to consist of 
approximately 12,000 gross square feet with retail and non-profit office space, but will no longer be 
constructed and will instead be incorporated as part of the revised Phase 3 Building, as detailed herein 
below. Under the Original Plan, the Phase 3 Building was approved as a 10-story, up to 160 foot tall 
building, with 161,500 gross square feet of office uses and including several trays of below grade 
parking totaling 185 vehicular spaces (the “Original Phase 3 Building”). This First Amendment to the 
Original Plan proposes the following changes: (1) removal of Building 1B from the Project, (2) increase the 
footprint of the Phase 3 Building to combine with that of Parcel 25 Phase 1B Project, and (3) subdivision 
of Parcel 25H related to associated increased land area as shown herein (the “Revised Project”). No 
changes are proposed to the other approved or constructed buildings or portions of the Site. The 
Proposed Project (as further described below) will be developed on the subdivided Parcel 25H which 
consists of approximately 32,144 square feet of vacant land, currently used for construction staging for 
Phase 2 of the Parcel 25 Project and surface parking for Phase 1A of the Parcel 25 project (the “Project 
Site”). 

The Parcel 25 Phase 1A project for Building 1A (“Building 1A”) was completed and occupied 
on a subdivided Parcel 25D of approximately 22,803 square feet and the Parcel 25 Phase 1A project 
includes 40 Low Income Housing Tax Credit (“LIHTC”) affordable rental apartments, with 16 surface 
parking spaces, approximately 26,753 square feet of non-profit office space, and 4,577 square feet of 
retail spaces. 
 
The Parcel 25 Phase 2 Project for Building 2 (“Building 2”) under the Original Plan is 
currently under construction and consists of a 100% affordable 46-unit LIHTC residential housing 
building with 29 below grade parking spaces. The Building 2 Project is located on subdivided Parcel 
25G, a site of approximately 21,755 square feet. 
 
The Original Plan, as amended by this First Amendment, sets forth the proposed location and 
appearance of structures, open spaces and landscaping, uses, densities and dimensions of structures, 
traffic circulation, parking and loading facilities, access to public transportation and other zoning 
requirements applicable to the Revised Project. 
 
Amendments to the Original Plan 
 
As set forth below, this First Amendment modifies the Original Plan to amend the Project for 
the construction of much needed affordable residences in place of the Original Phase 3 Building’s 
previously contemplated and approved 10-story, 161,500 gsf office building at a height of 160 feet 
with several trays of below grade parking totaling 185 spaces. This First Amendment will replace the 
Original Phase 3 Building with a new six (6) story, approximately 120,000 gsf building with up to 94 
affordable rental residences and 33 above ground parking spaces, including eight (8) spaces for the 
sole use of Proposed Project residents and the remaining 25 spaces as ancillary parking for the 
adjacent Parcel 25 Phase 1A project, including residential, office and retail spaces (the “Proposed 
Phase 3 Project”). Additionally, this First Amendment removes the Building 1B Project under the 
Original Plan.

Proposed Project Location, Phasing and Appearance of Structures 
 The Original Plan sets forth the Project Location, Phasing and Appearance of Structures to 
include a total development of up to 305,750 gross square feet with approximately 98,000 
gross square feet of residential space (88 apartments), approximately 10,000 gross square 
feet of retail space, approximately 196,500 gross square feet of office space, and 
approximately 1,250 gross square feet of community space, including a Building 1B of 
approximately 12,000 square feet and 36 feet in height, and a Building 3 of approximately 
161,500 gross square feet in Building 3 and up to 160 feet in height. The Original Plan also 
states a maximum of 201 parking spaces will be provided in a combination of surface parking 
and a below-grade parking garage. 
 
 This First Amendment hereby revises this section by removing Building 1B under the 
Original Plan altogether and revising the Building 3 portion of the project to a new six (6) 
story building of approximately 70 feet with approximately 120,000 gsf and up to 94 
affordable rental residences and 33 above ground parking spaces, including eight (8) spaces 
for the sole use of currently proposed Phase 3 Project residents and the remaining 25 spaces as 
ancillary parking for the adjacent Building 1A project, including residential, office and retail 
spaces (“Proposed Phase 3 Project” or “Building 3”). 
 
 This First Amendment also revises this section to provide for the following overall project 
description of a total development of up to 251,170 gross square feet with approximately 
219,840 gross square feet of residential space (180 units), approximately 4,577 gross square 
feet of retail space, and approximately 26,753 gross square feet of office space. 
 
 This First Amendment also revises the parking programming in the Original Plan to now 
include in the Proposed Phase 3 Project a total of 33 above ground parking spaces, including 
eight (8) spaces for the sole use of Proposed Phase 3 Project residents and the remaining 25 
spaces 

as ancillary parking for the adjacent Building 1A project, equaling an overall total of 16 
surface parking spaces and 62 garage spaces and a total of 78 parking spaces overall for the 
Revised Project. 
 
 The location and appearance of the Project Location, Phasing and Appearance of Structures 
was included in schematic plans included with the Original Plan within Exhibit C. 
 
 This First Amendment hereby amends Exhibit C – PDA Conceptual Plans with regard to 
Building 1B and /Building 3 and replaces those with the attached new Exhibit C hereto which 
provides updated schematic plans, renderings and elevations for the Proposed Phase 3 Project 
in comparison to the Original Phase 3 Project. 
 
Open Space and Landscaping 
 
 The Original Plan sets forth the Open Space and Landscaping for the Project to include a 
plaza of approximately 40 feet by 60 feet between Building 1B and Building 2, and 
approximately 120 feet by 35 feet during full completion of all phases between Building 2 
and Building 3. 
 
 This First Amendment hereby revises this section by connecting the previously proposed 
spaces into one larger contiguous space located between the Building 1A, the Building 2, 
and the Building 3. 
 
Commercial Subdistrict 
 
No changes. 
 
Proposed Uses 
 
 The Original Plan sets forth the Proposed Uses for the Project to include residential, office, 
retail, and community space and accessory uses thereto, and, at full build-out, to contain up 
to 201 parking spaces in both surface and a below-grade garage made available on a phased 
basis as the Project is developed. 
 
 This First Amendment hereby revises this section by revising the overall parking space 
number from 201 parking spaces to a total of 78 parking spaces overall for the Revised 
Project. The Proposed Uses remain the same other than to add Ancillary Parking as an 
Allowed Use under this First Amendment in order to allow for six (6) parking spaces at the 
Building 2 Project to be utilized for the Building 1A Project, and 25 spaces on the Project 
Site as part of the Proposed Phase 3 Project (once the various parcels are subdivided) as 
ancillary parking for the adjacent Building 1A Project. 
 
Densities 
 
 The Original Plan sets forth the Densities for the Project as anticipated FAR of 
approximately 1.07 for proposed Phase 1 and approximately 4.0 for the fully phased Project, 
but not to exceed an FAR of 5.0. 
 
 This First Amendment hereby revises this section by providing an as built FAR of 

approximately 3.40 for Phase 1 (on its now subdivided lot), an as built FAR of 
approximately 2.47 for Phase 2 (on its now subdivided lot), and a proposed FAR of 
approximately 3.73 for Phase 3 as part of the Proposed Phase 3 Project (on its now 
subdivided lot), for an overall FAR of approximately 3.06 for the fully phased Revised 
Project on the Site, still not to exceed the approved allowable FAR of 4.00 under the 
Original Plan or the allowable FAR of 5.00 under the CC-2 Subdistrict for a PDA. 
 
Proposed Traffic Circulation, Parking, and Loading Facilities 
 
 The Original Plan sets forth the Proposed Traffic Circulation, Parking, and Loading 
Facilities for the Project to include up to 201 spaces within a surface lot (accessible from 
Gurney Street) and underground garage (accessible from Station Street). The Original Plan 
also details that as part of Phase 3 of the Project, the surface parking for the first two phases 
will be reconfigured and supplemented with a parking garage below grade and below the 
Phase 3 office building. The Original Plan states that in Phase 1, approximately 56 spaces 
will be provided on a surface lot on the Site and that Phase 2 will be served with 
approximately 24 surface parking spaces. 
 
 This First Amendment hereby revises this section by amending the overall parking space 
number from 201 total parking spaces to 78 total overall parking spaces for the Revised 
Project, to include 16 surface parking spaces at the Building 1A Project, 29 parking spaces 
at the Building 2 Project, and 33 above ground parking spaces at the Proposed Phase 3 
Project, including eight (8) spaces for the sole use of Proposed Phase 3 Project residents 
and the remaining 25 spaces as ancillary parking for the adjacent Building 1A project. This 
First Amendment now provides for an overall total of 16 surface parking spaces and 62 
garage spaces for a total of 78 parking spaces for the Revised Project. 
 
 This First Amendment also notes that the Proposed Phase 3 Project is an all-affordable 
development project, and as such, no off-street parking is required pursuant to Zoning Text 
Amendment No. 454 dated December 22, 2021, which states that: “in the case of affordable 
residential housing, no off-street parking shall be required. Affordable residential housing 
shall be considered to describe those projects where at least 60% of the proposed residential 
units are income-restricted at or below 100% of Area Median Income (AMI), as defined by 
the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.”

Public Benefits 
 
 The Original Plan sets forth the Public Benefits with regard to the overall phased Project. 
 
 This First Amendment hereby revises this section by including updated Public Benefits with 
regard to the specific Proposed Phase 3 Project. In fulfillment of the objectives of Article 59, 
Sections 59-29 through 59-32 of the Code and meeting the requirements of Section 80C-4 of 
the Code, this First Amendment provides for the following benefits: 
 
o Completes the revitalization of Roxbury Crossing as a gateway to the Mission Hill 
neighborhood; 
o Creates up to 94 units of much-needed affordable residential rental housing units; 
o Introduces new neighborhood residents who will provide support to the local 
community and utilize local businesses; 
o Activates an underutilized site, replaces a 32,144 square foot vacant lot, and 
contributes to the future growth and stability of Roxbury Crossing; 
o Offers an opportunity for a transit-oriented location within walking distance of the 
Roxbury Crossing Orange Line Station, steps away from the MBTA bus stop with 
numerous bus routes along Tremont Street as well as the SW Corridor Park and bike 
path; 
o Continues a thoughtfully designed streetscape that improves and enhances the 
pedestrian landscape and experience at its completed pedestrian pathway that serves 
as a public open space and street edges through its use of natural vegetation and 
architectural elements; 
o Establishes a premier example of sustainable construction and development; 
o Temporarily creates many new jobs in the construction and building trade industries; 
o Adds new annual property taxes for the City of Boston; and 
o Includes 94 bicycle parking spaces. 
o Provides space for one 15-dock bike share station onsite upon issuance of Certificate 
of Occupancy for the NPC Phase 3 Project, with the Proponent to work with the 
Boston Transportation Department and the Boston Planning and Development 
Agency to site the station appropriately. Bike share stations may require 
Administrative Review by the Public Improvement Commission (“PIC”). 
o Design and implements accessible pedestrian ramps connecting the Site across 
Station Street to Mindoro Street. This mitigation measure is subject to city or state 
agency review as needed. PIC approvals for these proposed improvements shall be 
completed before building permit issuance for the Proposed Phase 3 Project. The 
physical mitigation improvements shall be completed upon Certificate of Occupancy 
for the Proposed Phase 3 Project.

Dear Chair Rojas and Members of the Board,
I write to you today in support of Phase 3 of the project at Parcel 25. As District Councilor for
Mission Hill, I am cognizant of the need for more housing in the neighborhood. Not just
housing, but housing for extremely low-, low, and moderate-income families and individuals.
This project will deliver 94 units of affordable housing at all the previously mentioned levels of
income, 70 of which are family sized units, ensuring that all families can afford to live in this
wonderful neighborhood.
I am also pleased to see this proposal brought forward by a steadfast partner and leader in the
neighborhood, Mission Hill Neighborhood Housing Services. They are committed to helping
Mission Hill retain its cultural, racial and economic diversity and to do that, additional workforce
housing needs to be provided.
This project also serves to finish the beautification of a once blighted corner near Roxbury
Crossing. This area serves as a gateway into the neighborhood. I hope that people stepping off
the Orange Line get to see a vibrant housing community instead of what is currently there.
For these reasons, I ask the board to vote in support of the proposal before you today.
Thank you,

Mission Hill Parcel 25 Phase 3- Boston Public Works Department Comments 
Included here are Boston Public Works Department comments for the Mission Hill Parcel 25 Phase 3 PNC. 
Project Specific Scope Considerations: 
The developer should coordinate with BPDA, BTD and PWD to develop safety and accessibility improvements for 
pedestrians. The developer should verify and reconstruct the existing pedestrian ramps and crossings as needed, 
specifically those at Gurney Street and Station Street intersection, Halleck Street and Station Street intersection, 
Mindoro Street and Station Street intersection. The developer should also coordinate with the Parks Department 
regarding the street tree plantings. 
Site Plan: 
The developer must provide an engineer's site plan at an appropriate engineering scale that shows curb 
functionality on both sides of all streets that abut the property. 
Construction Within The Public Right-of- Way (ROW): 
All proposed design and construction within the Public ROW shall conform to PWD Design Standards 
(https://www boston gov/departments/public-works/public-works-design-standards). Any non-standard materials 
(i.e. pavers, landscaping, bike racks, etc.) proposed within the Public ROW will require approval through the Public 
Improvement Commission (PIC) process and a fully executed License, Maintenance and Indemnification (LM&I) 
Agreement with the PIC. Please note that the comments below are specific to proposed work within the Public 
ROW. 
Sidewalks: 
The developer is responsible for the reconstruction of the sidewalks abutting the project and, wherever possible, to 
extend the limits to the nearest intersection to encourage and compliment pedestrian improvements and travel 
along all sidewalks within the ROW within and beyond the project limits. The reconstruction effort also must meet 
current Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)/Massachusetts Architectural Access Board (MB) guidelines, 
including the installation of new or reconstruction of existing pedestrian ramps at all corners of all intersections 
abutting the project site if not already constructed to ADA/MB compliance per Code of Massachusetts Regulations 
Title 521, Section 21 (https://www.mass.gov/requlations/521-CMR-21-curb-cuts). This includes converting apex 
ramps to perpendicular ramps at intersection corners and constructing or reconstructing reciprocal pedestrian 
ramps where applicable. Plans showing the extents of the proposed sidewalk improvements associated with this 
project must be submitted to the PWD Engineering Division for review and approval. Changes to any curb geometry 
will need to be reviewed and approved through the PIC. 
Please note that at signalized intersections, any alteration to pedestrian ramps may also require upgrading the 
traffic signal equipment to ensure that the signal post and pedestrian push button locations meet current ADA and 
Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD) requirements. Any changes to the traffic signal system must 
be coordinated and approved by BTD. 
All proposed sidewalk widths and cross-slopes must comply to both City of Boston and ADA/MB standards. 
The developer is encouraged to contact the City's Disabilities Commission to confirm compliant accessibility within 
the Public ROW. 
Driveway Curb Cuts: 
Any proposed driveway curb cuts within the Public ROW will need to be reviewed and approved by the PIC. All 
existing curb cuts that will no longer be utilized shall be closed.

Landscaping: 
The developer must seek approval from the Chief Landscape Architect with the Parks and Recreation Department 
for all landscape elements within the Public ROW. The landscaping program must accompany a LM&I with the 
PIC. 
Street Lighting: 
The developer must seek approval from the PWD Street Lighting Division, where needed, for all proposed street 
lighting to be installed by the developer. All proposed lighting within the Public ROW must be compatible with the 
area lighting to provide a consistent urban design. The developer should coordinate with the PWD Street Lighting 
Division for an assessment of any additional street lighting upgrades that are to be considered in conjunction with

are proposed to contain a City-owned street light system with underground conduit, the developer shall be 
responsible for installing shadow conduit adjacent to the street lighting system. Installation of shadow conduit and 
limits should be coordinated through the BPDA Smart Utilities team. 
Roadway: 
Based on the extent of construction activity, including utility connections and taps, the developer will be responsible 
for the full restoration of the roadway sections that immediately abut the property and, in some cases, to extend the 
limits of roadway restoration to the nearest intersection. A plan showing the extents and methods for roadway 
restoration shall be submitted to the PWD Engineering Division for review and approval. 
Additional Project Coordination: 
All projects must be entered into the City of Boston Utility Coordination Software (COBUCS) to review for any 
conflicts with other proposed projects within the Public ROW. The developer must coordinate with any existing 
projects within the same limits and receive clearance from PWD before commencing work. 
Green Infrastructure: 
The developer shall work with PWD, the Green Infrastructure Division, and the Boston Water and Sewer 
Commission (BWSC) to determine appropriate methods of green infrastructure and/or stormwater management 
systems within the Public ROW. The ongoing maintenance of such systems shall require an LM&I Agreement with 
the PIC. Effects of water infiltration with respect to the adjacent underpass structure and underground MBTA 
tunnels that may be negatively impacted by infiltration may impact the ability to install such systems and should be 
considered. Coordination with PWD and MBTA will be required. 
Resiliency: 
Proposed designs should follow the Boston Public Works Climate Resilient Design Guidelines 
(https://www boston,gov/environment-and-energy/c1imate-resilient-desiqn-quide1ines) where applicable.

PROJECT SITE AND BACKGROUND 
 
The Seaport Square Project site (the “Project Site”) consists of approximately 23.5 
acres of land, defined by an L-shaped series of development blocks and generally 
bounded by Northern Avenue and Seaport Boulevard (between Old Sleeper Street 
and Pier 4 Boulevard) and by Stillings Street, Boston Wharf Road, and Pier 4 
Boulevard and B Street (between Seaport Boulevard and Summer Street). In 2010, 
the Project received approval from the BPDA, under Article 80B of the Code, for the 
construction of approximately 6,335,200 square feet (“sf”) of Gross Floor Area 
(“GFA”) of mixed uses. The City of Boston Zoning Commission (the “BZC”) approved 
a Planned Development Area Development Plan for Planned Development Area No. 
78 on October 13, 2010 (the “Original PDA Plan”). 
 
Following the adoption of the Original PDA Plan, the Proponent’s predecessor-in-
interest, MS Boston Seaport, L.L.C. (the “Original Proponent”), constructed a number 
of public realm improvements, and conveyed Block A, Blocks B and C, Block H, Block 
K, Block J, Block L1, Block L2, and Blocks M1 and M2 to third party developers for the 
development of such Blocks. The development of those Blocks has been completed. 
 
The Proponent acquired the undeveloped Blocks and developed open spaces – 
Blocks D, F, G, L-3-L-6, N, P, and Q – in October 2015, and proposed an updated and 
enhanced vision for the district, detailed in a Notice of Project Change filed on 
February 7, 2017 and a Supplemental Impact Report filed on September 12, 2017 
(collectively, the “2017 NPC”). The Proponent filed an Amended and Restated 
Development Plan for Planned Development Area No. 78 (the “PDA Plan”) on

INCLUSIONARY DEVELOPMENT POLICY 
 
The Overall Project contemplates the development of up to 2,511 total residential 
units, including both for sale and rental units. These 2,511 residential units include 
1,911 units already constructed (the “Completed Units”) plus the 600 units currently 
proposed under the 2022 NPC (the “NPC Units”). 
 
The first 2,500 units developed within the Overall Project (including units constructed 
on the developed Blocks) shall be subject to the Inclusionary Development Policy 
("IDP") in effect at the time of the BPDA's approval of the Original Project in 2010, 
which was the IDP as amended on September 27, 2007 (the "2007 IDP"). All units 
within the Proposed Project other than the first 2,500 units of the Overall Project shall 
be subject to the IDP dated December 10, 2015 (the "2015 IDP"). For the creation of 
on-site IDP units, the 2007 IDP required at least 15% of the market rate units (which 
is also approximately 13.04340% of the total units), and the 2015 IDP requires 13% 
of the total units. As currently proposed the 2007 IDP shall apply to 2,500 units and 
the 2015 IDP shall apply to 11 units. This results in a total required minimum IDP 
obligation of 328 IDP units. 
 
Should the Overall Project contain more than 2,500 residential units the 2015 IDP 
shall apply to all units over the first 2,500 developed. As currently proposed, the 
Overall Project consisting of up to 2,511 is required to produce a minimum of 328 
IDP units. Of these 231 units are Completed Units leaving 97 more IDP units to be 
constructed as NPC Units. 
 
With regard to the Proposed Project, the Proponent has agreed to provide up to 170 
IDP units exceeding the required 97 IDP units that remain to be constructed. This 
will bring the total IDP obligation for the Overall Project to 401 IDP units exceeding 
the required 328 IDP units that must be included in the Overall Project. Subject to 
the approval of the BPDA, the Proponent may satisfy the remaining IDP requirement 
(i.e. 170 IDP units) in whole or in part through the construction of income-restricted 
units reserved for City of Boston/BPDA-certified artists ("Artist IDP Units"). 
 
The location of the IDP units will be finalized in conjunction with BPDA staff and 
outlined in an Affordable Housing Agreement ("AHA") or an Affordable Rental 
Housing Agreement and Restriction (“ARHAR"), and sales prices, rents, and income 
limits will be adjusted according to BPDA published maximum sales prices, rents, and 

 
10 
 
 
 
income limits, as based on HUD AMIs, available at the time of the initial sale or rental 
of the IDP units. With the exception of Artist IDP Units whose size, features and 
distribution shall be approved by the BPDA in conjunction with the Mayor’s Office of 
Arts and Culture, IDP units must be comparable to or exceed the size, design, and 
quality of market rate units in the Proposed Project, cannot be stacked or 
concentrated on the same floors, and must be consistent with or exceed bedroom 
counts relative the market rate units in the Residential Block in which the units are 
being provided. 
 
An AHA or ARHAR must be executed along with, or prior to, the issuance of the Partial 
Certification of Consistency for a residential Block. The Proponent must also submit 
Affirmative Marketing Plan(s) (the "Plan") for the Affordable Housing Agreement(s) to 
the Boston Fair Housing Commission and the BPDA. Preference will be given to 
applicants who meet the following criteria, weighted in the order below: 
 
(1) Boston Resident 
(2) Household Size (a minimum of one (1) person per bedroom); 
(3) First time homebuyer (for home ownership units only) 
(4) Boston Certified Artist (for Artist IDP Units only) 
 
Where a unit is built out for a specific disability (e.g., mobility or sensory), a 
preference will also be available to households with a person whose need matches 
the build out of the unit. The City of Boston Disabilities Commission shall assist the 
BPDA in determining eligibility for such a preference. 
 
The IDP units will not be marketed prior to the submission and approval of the Plan. 
Homeownership units may not be rented prior to sale to an eligible buyer. 
A deed restriction or covenant will be placed on the IDP units to maintain affordability 
for a total period of fifty (50) years (this includes thirty (30) years with a BPDA option 
to extend for an additional period of twenty (20) years). The household income of 
any subsequent renter or buyer of the IDP units during this fifty (50) year period must 
fall within the applicable income for each IDP Unit. The BPDA or its assigns or 
successors will monitor the ongoing affordability of the IDP units, The Proponent 
shall satisfy the IDP requirements set forth above by providing the required IDP units 
on-site.

Pursuant to Section 3-1A and Article 80C of the Zoning Code of the City of Boston (the

1. 
PDA Development Plan Background. On November 16, 2017, the Boston 
Redevelopment Authority, d/b/a the Boston Planning & Development Agency (“BPDA”) 
approved an amendment to the maps entitled “Zoning Districts City of Boston” to establish 
revised boundaries for Planned Development Area No. 78, and also approved an Amended and 
Restated Development Plan for Planned Development Area No. 78 (the “2017 Development 
Plan”). On December 13, 2017, the Boston Zoning Commission (the “Commission”) approved 
the map amendment and the 2017 Development Plan, which became effective on December 13, 
2017. The Development Plan provides for the redevelopment of an approximately 33.5 acre area 
of land (the “Site”) in the South Boston Waterfront District for a mixed-use project (the 
“Project”). Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to 
such terms in the 2017 Development Plan. The 2017 Development Plan, as amended by this First 
Amendment, is referred to herein as the “Development Plan”. 
2. 
Purpose of First Amendment to Development Plan. This First Amendment 
amends the 2017 Development Plan to reflect the elimination of the approved but not yet 
constructed retail building on Block F, the potential construction of a free-standing structure of 
up to approximately 2,000 square feet of Gross Floor Area to accommodate Civic/Community 
Users and Cultural Facilities (expected to be programmed in conjunction with the Massachusetts 
Fallen Heroes Memorial on Block F), and the creation of additional open space on Block F 
pursuant to the Open Space Election described in Section X of the Original Plan. This First 
Amendment also revises certain details of the residential program for the Project, to reflect 
currently-proposed uses of Block G, Block L3, and Block L6, and adjusts the timing of 
transportation monitoring studies to be conducted by the Proponent to reflect impacts of the 
COVID-19 pandemic on transit usage and vehicle traffic. 
This First Amendment also address the permissibility of certain uses within the Project. 
Specifically, this First Amendment allows Clinic Use and related uses, including medical clinics, 
medical spas, cosmetic surgery clinics, offices of dentists and orthodontists, and similar uses, as 
well as animal hospitals, kennels, caterer’s establishments and bakeries.

PROJECT SITE AND BACKGROUND 
 
The Seaport Square Project site (the “Project Site”) consists of approximately 23.5 
acres of land, defined by an L-shaped series of development blocks and generally 
bounded by Northern Avenue and Seaport Boulevard (between Old Sleeper Street 
and Pier 4 Boulevard) and by Stillings Street, Boston Wharf Road, and Pier 4 
Boulevard and B Street (between Seaport Boulevard and Summer Street). In 2010, 
the Project received approval from the BPDA, under Article 80B of the Code, for the 
construction of approximately 6,335,200 square feet (“sf”) of Gross Floor Area 
(“GFA”) of mixed uses. The City of Boston Zoning Commission (the “BZC”) approved 
a Planned Development Area Development Plan for Planned Development Area No. 
78 on October 13, 2010 (the “Original PDA Plan”). 
 
Following the adoption of the Original PDA Plan, the Proponent’s predecessor-in-
interest, MS Boston Seaport, L.L.C. (the “Original Proponent”), constructed a number 
of public realm improvements, and conveyed Block A, Blocks B and C, Block H, Block 
K, Block J, Block L1, Block L2, and Blocks M1 and M2 to third party developers for the 
development of such Blocks. The development of those Blocks has been completed. 
 
The Proponent acquired the undeveloped Blocks and developed open spaces – 
Blocks D, F, G, L-3-L-6, N, P, and Q – in October 2015, and proposed an updated and 
enhanced vision for the district, detailed in a Notice of Project Change filed on 
February 7, 2017 and a Supplemental Impact Report filed on September 12, 2017 
(collectively, the “2017 NPC”). The Proponent filed an Amended and Restated 
Development Plan for Planned Development Area No. 78 (the “PDA Plan”) on 
September 15, 2017. On November 16, 2017, the BPDA voted, pursuant to Section 
80A-6.2 of the Code, to authorize the issuance of a Determination Waiving Further 
Review of the 2017 NPC and approval of the project described in the 2017 NPC as a 
Development Impact Project, and the BPDA issued such determination on 
November 1, 2018 (the “2017 NPC Determination”). The BPDA also voted on 

 
4 
 
 
 
November 16, 2017 to recommend that the BZC approve the PDA Plan, and the BZC 
approved the PDA Plan on December 13, 2017. 
 
On September 10, 2019, the Proponent filed a Notice of Project Change (the “2019 
NPC”), proposing changes to the development program for the building to be 
constructed on Block N and reflecting other adjustments to building programs within 
the Project to reflect as-built or as-proposed conditions that had emerged since the 
approval of the 2017 NPC. On November 14, 2019, the BPDA voted, pursuant to 
Section 80A-6.2 of the Code, to authorize the issuance of a Determination Waiving 
Further Review of the 2019 NPC and approval of the project described in the 2019 
NPC, and the BPDA issued such determination on February 26, 2020 (the “2019 NPC 
Determination”). 
 
As described below, since its acquisition of certain Blocks within the Project Site, the 
Proponent has completed construction of Block L-4, and construction of Block N, 
Block L-5, and Block P is underway. 
 
The term “Overall Project” describes the totality of the structures and other 
improvements within the Project that have already been completed or are currently 
underway, as described in the 2017 NPC and the 2019 NPC.

approximately 1,460,572 sf. Currently, the Overall Project’s approvals allow the 
construction of 7,723,110 sf of GFA within the Overall Project, which included

2022 NPC AND THE FIRST AMENDMENT TO DEVELOPMENT PLAN 
 
On May 6, 2022, the Proponent filed a Notice of Project Change (the “2022 NPC”) and 
the First Amendment to Development Plan. The 2022 NPC proposes revised 
development programs for the final development sites of the Project – Blocks L-3, L-
6 and G – and proposes key changes to Block F, the site of Seaport Common, in order 
to advance the priorities of providing additional public open space, affordable 
housing, and job creation opportunities and reducing carbon emissions through 
reductions in the number of parking spaces currently approved for the Project (the 
“Proposed Project,” as further described below). 
 
Block F is the current site of District Hall and the Seaport Common open space. The 
2017 NPC and PDA Plan previously approved the construction of a three-story mixed-
use building of approximately 30,000 sf of GFA east of Seaport Common, and the 
expansion of the Seaport Common from approximately 36,000 sf to approximately 
40,000 sf of open space. In order to create much-needed open space, the Proponent 
will exercise the Open Space Election, as defined in the PDA Plan, by entirely 
eliminating the previously-approved, approximately 30,000 sf building and instead 
expanding and reconstructing Seaport Common to create approximately 60,000 total 
sf of contiguous, signature open space. The design of the newly expanded Seaport 
Common will be subject to BPDA design review in accordance with the PDA Plan, and 
will be informed by community input by soliciting public input at key design 
milestones, to ensure that Seaport Common remains a high-quality, functional, and 
people-first public open space.

INCLUSIONARY DEVELOPMENT POLICY 
 
The Overall Project contemplates the development of up to 2,511 total residential 
units, including both for sale and rental units. These 2,511 residential units include 
1,911 units already constructed (the “Completed Units”) plus the 600 units currently 
proposed under the 2022 NPC (the “NPC Units”). 
 
The first 2,500 units developed within the Overall Project (including units constructed 
on the developed Blocks) shall be subject to the Inclusionary Development Policy 
("IDP") in effect at the time of the BPDA's approval of the Original Project in 2010, 
which was the IDP as amended on September 27, 2007 (the "2007 IDP"). All units 
within the Proposed Project other than the first 2,500 units of the Overall Project shall 
be subject to the IDP dated December 10, 2015 (the "2015 IDP"). For the creation of 
on-site IDP units, the 2007 IDP required at least 15% of the market rate units (which 
is also approximately 13.04340% of the total units), and the 2015 IDP requires 13% 
of the total units. As currently proposed the 2007 IDP shall apply to 2,500 units and 
the 2015 IDP shall apply to 11 units. This results in a total required minimum IDP 
obligation of 328 IDP units. 
 
Should the Overall Project contain more than 2,500 residential units the 2015 IDP 
shall apply to all units over the first 2,500 developed. As currently proposed, the 
Overall Project consisting of up to 2,511 is required to produce a minimum of 328 
IDP units. Of these 231 units are Completed Units leaving 97 more IDP units to be 
constructed as NPC Units. 
 
With regard to the Proposed Project, the Proponent has agreed to provide up to 170 
IDP units exceeding the required 97 IDP units that remain to be constructed. This 
will bring the total IDP obligation for the Overall Project to 401 IDP units exceeding 
the required 328 IDP units that must be included in the Overall Project. Subject to 
the approval of the BPDA, the Proponent may satisfy the remaining IDP requirement 
(i.e. 170 IDP units) in whole or in part through the construction of income-restricted 
units reserved for City of Boston/BPDA-certified artists ("Artist IDP Units"). 
 
The location of the IDP units will be finalized in conjunction with BPDA staff and 
outlined in an Affordable Housing Agreement ("AHA") or an Affordable Rental 
Housing Agreement and Restriction (“ARHAR"), and sales prices, rents, and income 
limits will be adjusted according to BPDA published maximum sales prices, rents, and 

 
10 
 
 
 
income limits, as based on HUD AMIs, available at the time of the initial sale or rental 
of the IDP units. With the exception of Artist IDP Units whose size, features and 
distribution shall be approved by the BPDA in conjunction with the Mayor’s Office of 
Arts and Culture, IDP units must be comparable to or exceed the size, design, and 
quality of market rate units in the Proposed Project, cannot be stacked or 
concentrated on the same floors, and must be consistent with or exceed bedroom 
counts relative the market rate units in the Residential Block in which the units are 
being provided. 
 
An AHA or ARHAR must be executed along with, or prior to, the issuance of the Partial 
Certification of Consistency for a residential Block. The Proponent must also submit 
Affirmative Marketing Plan(s) (the "Plan") for the Affordable Housing Agreement(s) to 
the Boston Fair Housing Commission and the BPDA. Preference will be given to 
applicants who meet the following criteria, weighted in the order below: 
 
(1) Boston Resident 
(2) Household Size (a minimum of one (1) person per bedroom); 
(3) First time homebuyer (for home ownership units only) 
(4) Boston Certified Artist (for Artist IDP Units only) 
 
Where a unit is built out for a specific disability (e.g., mobility or sensory), a 
preference will also be available to households with a person whose need matches 
the build out of the unit. The City of Boston Disabilities Commission shall assist the 
BPDA in determining eligibility for such a preference. 
 
The IDP units will not be marketed prior to the submission and approval of the Plan. 
Homeownership units may not be rented prior to sale to an eligible buyer. 
A deed restriction or covenant will be placed on the IDP units to maintain affordability 
for a total period of fifty (50) years (this includes thirty (30) years with a BPDA option 
to extend for an additional period of twenty (20) years). The household income of 
any subsequent renter or buyer of the IDP units during this fifty (50) year period must 
fall within the applicable income for each IDP Unit. The BPDA or its assigns or 
successors will monitor the ongoing affordability of the IDP units, The Proponent 
shall satisfy the IDP requirements set forth above by providing the required IDP units 
on-site.

RESILIENCY & SUSTAINABILITY 
 
The 2022 NPC proposes multiple measures designed to increase the Proposed 
Project’s already significant commitment to environmental sustainability and 
resiliency: 
 
• Increase open space and remove pervious area on Block F to create a 
signature 1.4-acre public open space at the heart of the neighborhood. This 
newly expanded open space will yield significant climate change resiliency 
benefits, capturing additional stormwater and retaining it on site rather than 
discharging it immediately into the BWSC system. 
• Plant approximately 100 trees in connection with the Proposed Project to 
reduce the urban heat island effect, improve pedestrian comfort, and 
contribute to a robust urban tree canopy in the Seaport neighborhood. 
• Raise the target bar for LEED certification from Silver to Gold (v4.2) for the 
project described in the 2022 NPC. 
• Incorporate heat-recovery chiller plants in the Proposed Project to enhance 
overall building energy performance. 
• Comply with the then-current Article 37 requirements at the time each Block 
of the Proposed Project seeks BPDA Design Review approval.

PROJECT SITE AND BACKGROUND 
 
The Seaport Square Project site (the “Project Site”) consists of approximately 23.5 
acres of land, defined by an L-shaped series of development blocks and generally 
bounded by Northern Avenue and Seaport Boulevard (between Old Sleeper Street 
and Pier 4 Boulevard) and by Stillings Street, Boston Wharf Road, and Pier 4 
Boulevard and B Street (between Seaport Boulevard and Summer Street). In 2010, 
the Project received approval from the BPDA, under Article 80B of the Code, for the 
construction of approximately 6,335,200 square feet (“sf”) of Gross Floor Area 
(“GFA”) of mixed uses. The City of Boston Zoning Commission (the “BZC”) approved 
a Planned Development Area Development Plan for Planned Development Area No. 
78 on October 13, 2010 (the “Original PDA Plan”). 
 
Following the adoption of the Original PDA Plan, the Proponent’s predecessor-in-
interest, MS Boston Seaport, L.L.C. (the “Original Proponent”), constructed a number 
of public realm improvements, and conveyed Block A, Blocks B and C, Block H, Block 
K, Block J, Block L1, Block L2, and Blocks M1 and M2 to third party developers for the 
development of such Blocks. The development of those Blocks has been completed. 
 
The Proponent acquired the undeveloped Blocks and developed open spaces – 
Blocks D, F, G, L-3-L-6, N, P, and Q – in October 2015, and proposed an updated and 
enhanced vision for the district, detailed in a Notice of Project Change filed on 
February 7, 2017 and a Supplemental Impact Report filed on September 12, 2017 
(collectively, the “2017 NPC”). The Proponent filed an Amended and Restated 
Development Plan for Planned Development Area No. 78 (the “PDA Plan”) on 
September 15, 2017. On November 16, 2017, the BPDA voted, pursuant to Section 
80A-6.2 of the Code, to authorize the issuance of a Determination Waiving Further 
Review of the 2017 NPC and approval of the project described in the 2017 NPC as a 
Development Impact Project, and the BPDA issued such determination on 
November 1, 2018 (the “2017 NPC Determination”). The BPDA also voted on 

 
4 
 
 
 
November 16, 2017 to recommend that the BZC approve the PDA Plan, and the BZC 
approved the PDA Plan on December 13, 2017. 
 
On September 10, 2019, the Proponent filed a Notice of Project Change (the “2019 
NPC”), proposing changes to the development program for the building to be 
constructed on Block N and reflecting other adjustments to building programs within 
the Project to reflect as-built or as-proposed conditions that had emerged since the 
approval of the 2017 NPC. On November 14, 2019, the BPDA voted, pursuant to 
Section 80A-6.2 of the Code, to authorize the issuance of a Determination Waiving 
Further Review of the 2019 NPC and approval of the project described in the 2019 
NPC, and the BPDA issued such determination on February 26, 2020 (the “2019 NPC 
Determination”). 
 
As described below, since its acquisition of certain Blocks within the Project Site, the 
Proponent has completed construction of Block L-4, and construction of Block N, 
Block L-5, and Block P is underway. 
 
The term “Overall Project” describes the totality of the structures and other 
improvements within the Project that have already been completed or are currently 
underway, as described in the 2017 NPC and the 2019 NPC. 
 
The Project Site comprises approximately 1,023,396 sf; the PDA Plan area comprises 
approximately 1,460,572 sf. Currently, the Overall Project’s approvals allow the 
construction of 7,723,110 sf of GFA within the Overall Project, which included 
approximately 2.9 million sf of residential uses, approximately 3.3 million sf of
